utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Case number IT-95-9-T, the Prosecutor versus Blagoje Simic, Miroslav Tadic, and Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Cross-examination is continuing.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Weiner: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Simic.

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday when we left off, counsel -- Defence counsel asked me to, instead of one long question, break it up and ask you some shorter questions. So let's continue on this matter of the Vidovdan awards and decorations. Let's just go back, take it back a few steps. In early 1993 or sometime in -- early 1993, by that time, according to your testimony, you were aware of the Crkvina massacre of 16 civilians, 16 non-Serb civilians, correct?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were aware, at least from all the rumours and the stories, everything going around town, and the information you received, that Lugar and some fellow Serbian volunteers were alleged to have committed that crime?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you also indicated that you knew that Crni was some sort of commander of these volunteers or special battalion?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. A certain differentiation has to be made here. Crni was indeed one of the commanders of the special battalion, but I am not aware that Lugar was in this special battalion and in what formation he was anyway. So there is a difference.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you knew Lugar was not one of the locals?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. Lugar was not a local.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, in fact, you knew Crni and Lugar and this -- and some of these people were arrested in late 1992, and you thought it was due to the Crkvina killings, and you knew Crni was arrested.

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I did not know why they were arrested and what they were guilty of, each and every one of them. I don't know. I didn't know that. I assumed that Lugar was on account of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you testified that you believed that the reason for the arrest of Crni and some of the others had to do with the Crkvina killings. That was your testimony on the 29th of November, 2002, on Friday. Correct?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not say that that was the main reason. As a matter of fact, I said clearly that I did not know the exact and precise reasons, but I assumed that Lugar had been arrested on account of that, among other things, and that at any rate the military investigative authorities know about that crime of his. As for the others, I really did not know the reasons why they were there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But --

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What was also mentioned was the closing off of the corridor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Correct. The closing of the corridor. But you also mentioned that you assumed it had to do with Crkvina, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You've said yourself that what I did not see could only be speculations on my part. I cannot testify about something that I personally find unclear and vague.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, sir --

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But in your question --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You believed -- you testified that you believed that it had to do with certain military matters and Crkvina -- what you believed, based on what you heard. I'm not asking what exactly happened at those hearings. I'm not asking what did in fact happen, what complaints were issued. What you believe. And you testified that you thought or you assumed it had to do with Crkvina and the closing off of the corridor, correct?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you also stated that --

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And you also stated, sir, that you did not know the results of those proceedings. You don't know what resulted from those proceedings.

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, I did not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So in 1993 you did not know -- either late 1992 or 1993 you did not know the result of those proceedings, again, Crni, Lugar, the volunteers, and the whole group from Serbia.

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not know the outcome?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. However, in 1993, the Samac Municipal Assembly, of which you were a member, awarded Crni and Debeli St. Vitus decorations; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I have to say that I was opposition in that assembly, and that should be stated here. I cannot remember the exact outcome of that vote, but I can say the following, which is very important for this particular matter: In the country that I hail from, at least one out of every five persons has a decoration, an award of some kind. Statistically speaking, in the times of the socialist Yugoslavia --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- We're not going to get back to the socialist Yugoslavia. Sir, we discussed this for five to ten minutes yesterday --

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This award, this Vidovdan/St. Vitus Day decorations or awards. And at no time in that discussion yesterday did you ever mention that you were opposed -- you opposed that decision at the assembly. At no time yesterday. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not what I said. But it's very important to know the actual techniques involved in the adoption of such decisions. It is quite possible that I did not notice any such thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, again --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Weiner. I'd just like a clarification. The witness said on line 8 and following of page 4 that he wants us to know that he was -- to use his words, he says, "I was opposition in that assembly." Now, I think we need a clarification. Because from what I hear the witness saying, it seems as though he was in an opposition party. Your question, on the other hand, seems to be suggesting that he was opposing the awarding of the decorations. Those are two different things. So if -- perhaps if the witness could just clarify for us, that would settle that matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please clarify -- first, did you understand the Judge's comments, sir?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have understood.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us whether you opposed that particular decision or you were in an opposing party in the assembly.

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in an opposition party in the assembly, but I really cannot remember -- actually, as far as I can remember, there wasn't a debate. I don't remember how I voted, because the awarding of decorations is an irrelevant subject as far as I'm concerned. Precisely because of this hyperproduction of such diplomas. If you have several thousands of people with a certain kind of recognition, that devalues that particular award. That is my personal opinion. It is my personal opinion that such awards do not have much value. That is my personal view, and that's why I didn't pay much attention to this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When this decision was reached.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you testified --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you testified yesterday, and in the five to ten minutes we discussed this issue you never stated that these were devalued awards, that your opinion were that these were some sort of negligible awards or devalued awards. You never said that yesterday, sir; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I probably didn't have enough time to say that, but I'm saying it right now. If several thousand awards are given --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In a period --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't say it yesterday. That's the question.

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I certainly did not have time to say everything valuing the time that I have available here, but I am saying it right now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you didn't say it yesterday; yes or no? It's a simple question.

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I didn't say it. But let it be. I didn't say it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And will you agree that the decoration was awarded to those two people, Crni and Debeli, for the successful command and control of units of the Army of the Republika Srpska, the defence of the people and Serbian land?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would appreciate it if I could see that document again.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: 126A, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Can it be shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: For the sake of clarity, it should be P126, yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: P126. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which Official Gazette and which page?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's section 35, Article 2, decision of 24 June 1993.

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you kindly give me the number of the Official Gazette.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's on page 3 or 4, sir. It's page 1 in the English. 46/93. We can find it for you, if you'd like, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Maybe the usher can assist.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I've found it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I invite your attention to Article 2, "Decorations shall be awarded to the following for the successful command and control of units of the Army of the Republika Srpska, the defence of the people and Serbian land." And those were given to Crni and Debeli, correct?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, if you look at Article 5, some additional awards were also given. Awards were given to Blagoje Simic, Milan Simic, Stevan Todorovic, and Mirko Lukic. It says, "Shall be awarded decorations for their selfless contribution to the struggle for freedom and the defence of the Republika Srpska." Is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you've read it correctly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that was signed by Dr. Blagoje Simic, president of the municipal assembly.

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's signed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And those awards were given to them on the 30th of June in 1993 by the Serbian -- I'm sorry, the Serbian Assembly of the Samac Municipality, correct?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Assembly of the Municipality of Samac. The Assembly of the Municipality of Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And they were awarded for their selfless contribution to the struggle for freedom and the defence of the Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's move on. You testified on Thursday, the 28th of November, 1992 -- I'm sorry, the 28th of November, 2002, that you learned sometime, I assume in March, that in late February of 1992 an assembly of the Serbian people was held. That was your testimony, correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I would be very grateful if we could have a page transcript of these parts so that we can follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, 12.988.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that your testimony, sir, that you were aware --

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you further testified that an Assembly of the Serbian People of Bosanski Samac and Pelagicevo under formation was established, correct?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I said that I learned that the assembly had been established. However, I could not have found out about that towards the end of February because it had been founded towards the end of February. I found out later. But perhaps that is insignificant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. I totally agree. You testified you found out later. Now, you also testified that none of the bodies from that assembly ever functioned later, nor did that assembly ever function in a true sense. Those were your words; isn't that correct? Also at pages 1 -- I'm sorry, 12.988. That was your testimony.

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I'm not aware that the authorities, even if they were elected by that assembly, but I don't know about that, that they were never proclaimed elected by that assembly or did they ever start operating as such.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, let's talk about that. Isn't it true that Ilija Ristic was elected president of the Municipal Assembly of Bosanski Samac and Pelagicevo under formation on February 29th, 1992? Isn't that true, sir?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only say that I had heard about him being elected. So if this is not considered to be a speculation, then I can say it. I was not an eyewitness of this event, but I heard about it later on. I could read it in Official Gazettes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And that was in fact listed in the Official Gazette.

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I read it in the Official Gazettes only in 1994/1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And are you also aware that plans were developed for the formation of municipal government bodies at the assembly, that those plans were developed and continued to be developed later, such as the rules and duties of the president, vice-president, secretary of the municipal assembly, and plans for the working bodies were also described, and the election procedures were also developed or formulated? Were you also aware of that from reading the Official Gazette in 1994?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I saw that in Official Gazettes, and I saw that there was total confusion there. And to be quite frank, I didn't understand any of those documents. Who did what, who was in charge of what, all of that was --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The issue is not whether you understood it. The issue was weren't those plans made; that's the question. Whether you personally understood it or agreed with it, that's not of consequence here. The issue is or the question is: Were those plans made? You said you saw them in the gazette.

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Official Gazettes, there are such things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And isn't it also true that it was published in the gazette in March of 1992. Stevan Todorovic was elected chief of the Public Security Station of the Serbian Municipality of Samac by that Assembly of the Serbian Municipality of Samac? Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we are speaking about the Official Gazette and some other documents, it would be fair for the witness to have this particular Official Gazette in front of him and -- because there is a lot of regulations in one gazette, so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's gazette 124, since he's indicated he has seen them, I haven't asked to have it be placed in front of him. But I would be happy to let him see P124. P124.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, please, as much as possible let the witness get the documents being discussed. Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would also like to draw your attention to the fact that the Prosecutor on page 10, line 15, said that this was published in the Official Gazette in March 1992. And the Prosecutor knows him full well that this is not correct. That it was only in March 1993 -- or rather, 1994. So could the Prosecutor please be accurate when he is saying when something was published, not when the actual decision was made.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: What line are you referring to, sir?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'm very familiar it's June 1994. I don't recall saying 1992. I'm sorry. I'm sorry, it was a slip of the tongue. It was -- he was elected chief in March of 1992. That's not when the gazette was published.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, are you aware that Stevan Todorovic was elected chief of the Public Security Station of the Serbian Municipality of Bosanski Samac by that assembly and he was elected in March of 1992? It's on page 12 of the English, Article 1. It's a list of persons elected to the executive council. So do you agree that Stevan Todorovic was elected by the Samac Municipal Assembly in March of 1992, sir?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Official Gazette I see that that is the way it was, but I have no other knowledge concerning that. Now, whether this Official Gazette is authentic or not is something I cannot assess.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, that's not an -- that's not your job to make that assessment. It's already been -- it has already been admitted as an exhibit in this case, sir. However, does it indicate at Article 1 that Stevan Todorovic was elected Chief of the Public Security Station by that Samac Municipal Assembly?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says decision on the election of members of the executive board and the name of Mr. Stevan Todorovic is here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And sir, doesn't it also indicate that that Samac Municipal Assembly and Pelagicevo under formation elected 10 additional members to the executive council of that assembly? You can count them if you'd like, for a total of 11.

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are 11 names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of persons elected by the municipal assembly -- by the Samac Municipal Assembly, correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the preamble it says that that is the Assembly of the Municipality of Samac and Pelagicevo under formation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And they elected the members of -- those 11 members of the executive council. That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what is written here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, further -- isn't it also true, sir, that the assembly charged the new executive council president and those senior officials to organise the work of the organs of administration and to carry out preparations for the transition to work under wartime conditions? If you look at the next page. Isn't that true? Weren't those persons ordered to do that by the municipal assembly? Article 2.

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, isn't it further true that in March of 1992 - and this is not from this document. This is from the testimony of Blagoje Simic - that in March of 1992 it was decided that a Crisis Staff should be established -- a Crisis Staff should be established in the Serbian Municipality of Bosanski Samac if war breaks out in the Posavina and the president and vice-president of the municipality, as well as the chairman of the municipal board of the SDS, were responsible for implementing that decision of establishing a Crisis Staff? Are you aware of that, sir?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know why I am supposed to testify about a document that already exists and that was already admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, that's not the question. My question to you is: Are you aware, according to the testimony of Blagoje Simic, that also in March of 1992 it was decided that the Crisis Staff should be established in the Serbian Municipality of Bosanski Samac if war breaks out in the Posavina and the president and vice-president of the municipality, as well as the chairman of the municipal board of the SDS, were responsible for implementing that decision? Are you aware of that, sir?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't present at that assembly and I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Sir, isn't it a fact that in mid-April 1992 a Municipal Crisis Staff was established for the municipality of Bosanski Samac? You were a member of that, so you should be aware that it was in fact established.

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, are you also aware that Dr. Blagoje Simic, president of the municipal chapter of the SDS was appointed president of that Crisis Staff, of the Serbian Municipality of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dr. Blagoje Simic was appointed president of the Crisis Staff of Samac Municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Finally - and that's also stated in that document on pages 21 and 22 in the English - do you agree that on April 14th and 15th, the executive council of the Serbian Municipality of Bosanski Samac and Pelagicevo under formation concluded that the Chief of the Public Security Station should immediately establish a special purpose unit of the MUP to work with the military and civilian authorities to protect the Serbian people? Are you aware of that, sir? It's stated at pages 21 and 22.

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware that any special unit had been established, nor do I know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, are you aware that two defendants in the case have given statements to the OTP where they have described the activities of the Serbian police unit during the takeover and immediately after the takeover of Bosanski Samac? Are you aware of that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. It is too general assumption. The witness cannot say what the defendants say. Maybe my learned friend can be more specific. When? How? Who said what? This is very, very general. It's confusing the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's not confusing him. I'm just asking him if he's aware. He made statements that nothing ever came from this assembly. Apparently a number of decisions came from the assembly. And I'm asking him if he's aware of certain activity. He can say yes or he can say no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, I think in fairness to the witness, it's better to reiterate -- go back to those statements. They're already on record. And remind -- and refresh the mind of the witness. I think he has been giving evidence for quite some time and he has seen so many documents. So in fairness to the witness, it's always better to be precise, show the document, read out the statement, so that the witness is able to direct his mind to the evidence which is under discussion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Additionally, Mr. Weiner, I'm just wondering, how would this witness know what was in statements that two of the accused persons gave to the OTP?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: We've been reading out statements that have been given to the OTP for the last several days. And in addition to that, some of these statements were also publicly made to newspapers and publicly made within the communities. It was public -- all I'm saying is it was public knowledge that the Serbian police were involved in the takeover of Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Just for the record, this is pure speculation from the part of the Prosecution, because he cannot even say when it was published, who said what. So just for the record. Nothing more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to read a statement from Miroslav Tadic, his statement to the Prosecutor at page 24 -- the statement of 26 March 1998, Exhibit 138.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe it would be fair to the witness if an evidence is put to him and here we have something that had been admitted into evidence -- to have that interview put before the witness and especially this segment in which the Prosecutor is interested and in the language of the witness. I'm saying this because I have noticed that when the Prosecutor was reading out segments of the interview of Miroslav Tadic, the Prosecutor was taking it out of context and putting only some sentences and some phrases from the interview, having previously taken them out of context. This is why I believe that it would be fair to the witness to have the interview put in front of him so that he could see it as well as everybody else in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner. I think it's only to try and help the witness to direct his mind to what is being discussed, because all these documents are already on record.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] We have them. Your Honour, we have copies with the B/C/S -- English and B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: However, I would state -- I'd strongly object to the statement made by counsel that we were taking things out of context. We read what was stated. Your Honour, I'd like to move these statements into evidence. These statements correspond to each one that's already been admitted. The only thing is they have the English and then they have directly under that the B/C/S. It's the exact same. It's just the B/C/S translation of the English, so it's kind of a -- it's a joint document, English and B/C/S, of the document that's already in evidence. That one there is document 138.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Have the Defence been given? Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we are very grateful to the Prosecution for having created interviews in this form. We saw that with respect to Stevan Todorovic that there have been certain differences. I would like this document to receive an identification number because we are currently conducting comparison of these translations. I don't think it would turn into a problem, but it would be useful to us if this document was identified with an identification number because we are currently conducting comparisons of translations.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No objection to that. Let them take whatever time they'd like to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner, what we're trying to clarify here is that we've already got these interviews into evidence in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes, we do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What you have now is the B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So we're only admitting these as the B/C/S version?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yeah, you could admit it as a B/C/S or a joint B/C/S-English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. Because we can't have a document admitted twice.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No, fine. Just the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: In this case then they'll with given identification -- they'll be admitted as exhibits. The questions of incorrect or correct translation can be dealt with.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I just want to ask you to look at the top of page 34. And could you just follow along one question with me. The first question: "Q. Who managed to take over the town of Bosanski Samac then if the 4th Detachment was not involved? Answer by Mr. Tadic: "It was not a problem to take over Bosanski Samac. There was the Serbian police, some trained people, and in a half hour they took over Bosanski Samac without any shots being fired, without shelling, without the war." Is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. All I know is that the shooting lasted for several days and practically didn't stop. I don't know anything about that half an hour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I just read to you, was that correct, sir? What I just said to you, did I read it properly?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mostly, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, sir, when you said that no actions were taken as a result of that assembly, you were wrong, because the assembly did in fact take actions, as you see in that gazette. A number of actions had been taken.

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I was wrong. Perhaps some of the members took actions, some members of the executive council. However, I'm not aware of the fact that the executive council ever convened in that composition. I'm not aware of that. I don't even think that that is reflected -- these actions are reflected in the Official Gazette.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now, as to whether some of these people were included --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, weren't actions taken as a result of the municipal assembly? Weren't actions taken? They established an executive board. They placed people on there. Weren't actions and decisions taken, as you've read -- and you say you've noticed and you've read in the gazette? Weren't actions taken?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I read in the Official Gazette, I cannot claim that they took any actions based on that. On the contrary, I can see --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, the fact that they made decisions to appoint people and establish boards, weren't those decisions taken? Didn't they make some decisions? They established a Crisis Staff. Isn't that a decision?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are a number of questions that stem from that, and I am unable to give you an answer that would cover all of these questions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Then let's move on to another question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: If the witness could be shown P145A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we have a number for this B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes. It will be Exhibit P138 ter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Ter ID?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. I did say that it would be admitted into evidence as an exhibit. If there are problems with translation, that will be dealt with during the trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I may address just to the registry. Just to make sure what we are talking about. Because we had interviews of Mr. Zaric -- three interviews of Mr. Zaric. And we also have two interviews of Mr. Tadic. So this particular document, are we talking about first or second interview with Mr. Tadic? Because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I think it's dated. The one the Bench has is dated, "Interview on 26 March 1998. "

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: That's the first interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The first interview. Okay. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: As we use the documents, each of the others, I can introduce those or can I just introduce those in lump, the other three interviews now, whichever the Court would like.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I think it's better to introduce them by numbers and also cite the date so that we are all clear which document we are discussing.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Would you like them all at this time or as we ...?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. As you deal with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, that's a copy of the Variant A and B document which you discussed previously in your testimony. What I'd like to tell you is --

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't speak about this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You testified previously that you were not aware of the document; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true. That means that I didn't discuss the document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't discuss the document. Correct. What I'm trying to say to you, sir: All of these decisions that we just discussed, nine decisions, the establishment of an assembly, the election of a police chief, the establishment of a Crisis Staff, these eight or nine decisions we just talked about which I asked you were you aware of each of those, the ones we just talked about, sir, are you aware that all nine of those decisions are required acts under Variant B of the Variant A and B document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I must -- I must object. This witness said that he is not aware of this Variant A and B, so how he can now make any conclusion or assumption with regard to certain preposition -- certain, I would say, theory -- Prosecution case theory?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no. Let him answer. If he can't, he will say so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware that all of those actions we've just discussed that were taken - the establishment of the municipal assembly and all the actions by the municipal assembly and the executive board - were all required under the Variant B section of the Variant A and B document? Are you aware of that, sir?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot be aware of something that I haven't read, and I especially cannot compare something that I didn't see with something from the Official Gazette. I don't know about this document, neither about Variant A, B, nor C, nor any other that you might mention.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, if you've never looked at the document -- hasn't counsel shown you that document before you got on the witness stand?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He showed it to me; however, I had no desire to read it. What would my motive be to read the document?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, what would your motive be? How can you say that you did not discuss and make decisions on the content of that document if you haven't looked at it to know exactly what the document contains?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can say that I have never discussed this document anywhere, because I will repeat this again, I am not familiar with this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, if you've never examined the document, examined the contents, how can you say you've never discussed any of the contents of it if you haven't looked at it? It's a long document.

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on the theory of coincidence, you might be right. But this is just guessing. This is just a speculation. It is possible that something that is mentioned in that document was accidentally mentioned by me sometimes; however, it is quite plausible that I know nothing about this document because on page 1 it says "Confidential Document of the Serb Democratic Party." So how could I be aware of something that has been classified?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, once again, how can you say that you didn't take the actions required in that document, you weren't involved in the actions required in that document, if you have not read the contents of the document?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have neither read the document nor have I taken any action regarding that document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you --

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I'm very confused by your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, if you've never read the document, you don't know what's contained in the document. Therefore, you can't state whether you've taken any actions based on that document -- based on the contents of that document.

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't read "Marxist Capital." So I can't tell you whether I've taken any action stemming from that book.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, then sir, you will not disagree with me -- so you cannot disagree with me when I say to you that nine of the actions which we just discussed moments ago which were taken by the assembly -- the Serbian Assembly of Bosanski Samac and Pelagicevo under formation were required to be taken under the Variant B section of the Variant A and B document. Then you cannot disagree with me on that when I give you that statement.

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What you've told me doesn't mean that I through my personal knowledge or through my experience reached that conclusion. If you're asking me to testify about your own analysis, that is not something that I deduced myself, then I'm unable to do that as a witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's move on, sir. Sir, you testified previously that you were the information officer for the Crisis Staff. You were the director of information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, maybe it's a matter of translation. They're confusing the terms here. Information officer, director of information. Why we can't simply say member of the Crisis Staff in charge of information, something like that. Because otherwise it won't be logical for the transcript, and the transcript is the evidence finally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So what you're saying is --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Because the witness is not hearing the word "information officer" in B/C/S language. He's hearing, "A member of Crisis Staff in charge for information." But in the transcript, contrary we have "information officer," "director for information," "chairman, or "CEO of information," "director," et cetera. I mean, I think my learned friend is a little bit pumping up, you know, this function. So let's stick to the issue: Member of the Crisis Staff in charge for information. And let's use that term, because otherwise he's confusing with the translation that he is receiving after these submissions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] I'd be very happy to use that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, please use the correct term.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you were a member of the Crisis Staff in charge of information, sir?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was a member of the Crisis Staff in charge of information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were the person who had to disseminate information, meet with the press, get information out to the press?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't exactly like that. Yesterday I explained that, and I don't think it is necessary for me to waste the time on that once again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. That's what I was about to say, that we had that explained in detail from the witness already.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, as part of your job -- actually, we've move on. Sir, you talked about a journalist, Mato Krajinovic, a -- I believe he's a Croatian journalist?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you indicated that he was involved in a propaganda ploy, correct?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't use that term. I don't know if this is a problem with translation. I don't think that it was a propaganda plot. But at any rate, he was one of the promoters of propaganda on the Croatian side in the radio station of Odzak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I said "propaganda ploy," not "propaganda plot." But he was using propaganda. And would you agree, sir, that the Croatians -- the Croatian government, the Croatians were using propaganda during the war.

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The media used it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, the Croatian media.

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One could hear this in the media.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Correct. And it was used to vilify or blame the Serbs or make people hostile to the Serbs, to make the Croats and Muslims hostile towards the Serbs, vilify them?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. Their objective was to portray Serbs in as bad a light as possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were aware that the Muslims, the Muslim media, the Muslim government was also using propaganda to their advantage?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, a similar thing can be said about the Muslim media.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And they were also portraying the Serbs in a bad light, correct?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most often, yes. Although, there are exceptions. One cannot generalise matters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And are you also aware that the Serb media was using propaganda during the war?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Serb media also used certain means of propaganda war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that was also to boost the morale of the Serb population and also to place the Muslims and Croats in a poor light.

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When it comes to the Samac municipality, this was taken into account. I can't speak of any higher levels, but I know for a fact that information and dissemination of information in Samac municipality on the part of the people who participated in that was as far as that was possible, it was professional and professionally done. Our publishing houses, our media at that time did not -- and we are talking about the first couple of months, at the beginning of the war. The system -- the information system didn't work properly, and in Samac we used as much as that was possible, we used information, i.e., the paper that was prescribed by the Pentagon for information during the Desert Storm. So from that document, we learned what could be published, what couldn't be published, and so on and so forth, and we believe that these were the highest professional standards.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It is absolutely a hundred per cent, a million per cent, contrary -- the transcript does not reflect what the witness said, and it's a very dangerous thing on a very sensitive issue, a very sensitive question. I will give you illustration. The question was: "And that was also to boost the morale of the Serb population and also to place the Muslim and Croats in a poor light." And then we are -- when we are reading the answer, it's absolutely contrary what the witness said, so I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Which line?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It's line 17. And until -- from page 26, line 17 until the line 4 of the next page. I don't want to say what I heard from this witness. I just want this witness to repeat the answer and also to hear the question, because it's a very, very serious thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, at that point -- I was going to stop the witness anyway, because it's not responsive to the answer. I asked him --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No. Please, I want this part to be strike from the transcript, because it does not correspond to the what the witness said. So please, could you pose another -- the same question and then let's hear the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the answer is not responsive to my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. What the -- Mr. Pantelic is saying is that the translation is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: If he -- if you'd like to strike it, that's fine. It's not responsive. I don't care if you want to strike. It's not responsive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay. Then it will be struck off record.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Fine. It's not responsive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, my question again was: The Serbian media used propaganda placing the Muslims and the Croats in a bad light, just as the others did; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We cannot generalise as I have already said about the Croatian and the Muslim media.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, isn't it true that the Serb media was distorting information and placing the Muslims and the Croats in a bad light? Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a very general definition, and I cannot answer that question of yours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isn't it true that segments -- we'll do it your way -- segments of the Serb media were using propaganda and placing the Muslims and Croats in a bad light?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please be more precise and tell me exactly what document, when was it published, on which page.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, in general, wasn't the Serb media just like the Muslim media and the Croatian media, using propaganda, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The use of the media was similar, to my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So just as the Muslims and Croats were using propaganda, so was the Serb media using propaganda.

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't study the media and what the media carried on any of the sides. I can just give you my impressions, and my impression is that the reporting in the media was more or less similar, because they all used the similar methods. But that is just my impression. I did not particularly study the media, nor am I aware of any of the results of any of the studies that would have me in the media at that time as their subject.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We've spent a lot of time on this, Mr. Weiner. Can we move on?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, it's going to be my allegation that he was the propaganda ideologue for the Bosanski Samac. That's why I'm trying to spend some time on this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well. Then move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you were appointed by the municipality's executive council as editor-in-chief of "Koridor" magazine; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Koridor" magazine had three editors-in-chief while it existed, and I was one of the editors-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in addition to being editor-in-chief of "Koridor" -- one of the editors-in-chief of "Koridor" magazine, you were also appointed director of the municipal public information company in 1993? You were appointed the director of that?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And under the municipal public information company -- I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From January to April 1993 I was the principal of the secondary school. And from April 1993 onwards, I was the director of Duga public company and the information services was just one of the segments of that company, and you can see that in the decision.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And information services was involved. In fact, you oversaw the press, the TV, and the radio as part of the umbrella of that information services.

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That company had information as one of the segments. Then there was a library. There was a cultural centre, and there was also catering. These were all the segments of that company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- Sir. You oversaw the press, the TV, and the radio as part of the information services' umbrella.

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid that we will have to study the law in order to answer that question. In addition to the director, who was also a manager, there were also editors-in-chief of the various media. I was at the same time the editor-in-chief of "Koridor" and the editor of the radio station was somebody else, and he was responsible before the law for the things that were aired by that radio station.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I have a few minutes to get a document I need on this issue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] How many minutes, Mr. Weiner?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Five minutes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well. We'll rise for five minutes. --- Break taken at 10.40 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, in addition to being director of the municipal public information company, you indicated that you were the -- one of the editors-in-chief of the magazine "Koridor," a bimonthly magazine. Wasn't one of the uses of "Koridor" magazine for the purposes of propaganda? Wasn't that one of the uses of "Koridor" magazine?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you look at the Official Gazettes carefully, you will see it clearly that the editorial policy to defined there, but propaganda activity isn't mentioned anywhere, and you can easily see that in the Official Gazettes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We're going to get to that, sir. Sir, weren't you required to discuss topics such as war crimes and genocide against the Serbian people? Weren't you required to discuss that in the magazine?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please explain who would it have been who asked for that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, the magazine was established by the municipality. Didn't the municipality municipal assembly require that you discuss topics such as war crimes and genocide against the Serbian people? Wasn't that the required -- part of the required content of that magazine? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The municipal assembly as the founder defined its position, i.e., the global editorial concept, and it did that in its act on the establishment of the magazine, and later on it was the editorial board which was in charge of putting the magazine together in keeping with the professional norms and standards of journalism. And as such, editors-in-chief and journalists, together with the editor-in-chief, were responsible for ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's not my question. My question was: Didn't the municipal assembly require that you discuss topics such as war crimes and genocide against the Serbian people? Weren't you required to do that by the municipal assembly?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I repeat: The municipal assembly issued a document to define that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, once again, my question was: Were you required to discuss topics such as war crimes and genocide against the Serbian people? That's my question. Yes or no, or you can't answer it? Say you don't know.

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I do know, but that was just one of the segments in the content of this magazine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were required to discuss in your magazine war crimes and genocide against the Serbian people. You agree with me. Correct?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Every topic of public significance could find a place in this magazine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, the question is: You were required to discuss in your magazine war crimes and genocide against the Serbian people. That was part of the content that the municipal assembly told you you had to include; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see this question as too acute, too pronounced. That could have been one of the topics.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, was another topic that you were required to place in your magazine discussions of the combat-readiness of the Army of Republika Srpska? Were you also required to place that in your magazine, stories about that?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On our team of journalists, we did not have an expert on military issues, so in that part I believe that there were not many articles. I can't remember right now, but it is possible. Journalists would write stories from the front lines and from the life of soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, isn't it true that the Municipal Assembly of Bosanski Samac told you or determined the content of "Koridor" magazine? They determined for you what the content of "Koridor" magazine would be; isn't that true, sir?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said that the document to establish "Koridor" magazine also contains a passage which defines the global editorial policy, but it is a very general passage in that document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, didn't they determine the -- not the global editorial policy but the overall content of the magazine? Didn't they determine the overall content for you?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be wrong if somebody dictated what journalists should write. A journalist has to be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You were not asked on the general forum. It's specific question whether the assembly directed the contents of the magazine. Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The municipal assembly did not determine the contents of the magazine.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may the witness be shown Exhibit P125, please, in the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Section 19, Article 4. In the English, it's page 11, the decision on the founding of "Koridor" magazine. Could you please look at that, go to that. Do you have that, sir?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I've found it, and this is exactly what I was talking about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's exactly what I was talking about too. Could we go to paragraph 3 of Article 4. Do you see that? And I'd like to read that, and would you please tell me if I'm reading it correctly. "In terms of its content, 'Koridor' shall be organised to facilitate the clarification and affirmation of the current military and political situation of the Serbian people of the Sava Valley and also in the territory of the former Bosnia and Herzegovina and Croatia. All of the magazine's contents from war reports and documentary photographic material to commentaries shall be completely oriented towards the affirmation of the genuine interest of the Serbian people and the moral profile of the combat-readiness of the Army of the Republika Srpska. The publication shall also follow all economic, political, and cultural events in the Sava Valley and also the social situation caused by the war." Finally: "'Koridor' shall contain features on the gathering of material evidence of war crimes and crimes of genocide committed against the Serbian population of the region." Is that correct? They dictated what the content of that magazine should be, the overall content, sir?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They defined the editorial principles, but they did not dictate the content. The editorial policy and the editorial content are two different things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, doesn't it state that "'Koridor' shall contain features on the gathering of material evidence of war crimes and crimes of genocide committed against the Serbian population of this region"? That's what it says there. That's what it shall contain, correct? And it also says that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Let the witness --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it says also, "The magazine's content" -- all of the magazine's contents, from war reports and documentary, photographic material to commentaries,"shall be completely" -- and look at the word --"oriented toward the affirmation of the genuine interest of the Serbian people and the moral profile of the combat-readiness of the Army of the Republika Srpska." That's what they told you. That's what it shall be oriented towards. Correct?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document was drafted by somebody from the administration, and that's why it is what it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that was an order that was signed by Dr. Blagoje Simic, president of the municipal assembly, on the 17th of April in 1993.

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not an order. An order is a military term, and this is a decision passed by the municipal assembly for which 50 MPs in the assembly voted. And whatever they voted for was later on by the president of that assembly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see the word "order" anywhere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that decision indicated that -- what the contents, the overall contents of the magazine should be. That decision -- whether you want to call it an order or a decision. Use your term "decision." That indicated what the contents of the magazine would be.

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not my term. It is an administrative term in the municipal assembly, and I repeat, the programme concept and the contents of a magazine are two different things. Everywhere the founder has the right to define the editorial policy, and the contents of the magazine are defined by the team of its journalists, and that is the only answer to that that I can give you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we take our break?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And Mr. Weiner, you've had your time, actually, in cross-examination. We started yesterday at 12.00, so you should be winding up. We'll continue at 11.30 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Sir, are you aware that in 1993 a new television station, Studio Samac, was also established by the Serbian Municipality -- the Serbian Municipal Assembly? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Municipality of Samac passed a decision on the establishment of a TV station, Studio Samac, but that TV station did not start operating until 1996. It didn't work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But it did in 1993 establish a television station?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The foundation act was passed in accordance with legal regulations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it placed it within the framework of Duga, which you were the director of, the informational agency.

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That TV station was not stationed anywhere because it did not have any equipment. I repeat, that --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, sir. That's not my question. My questions was: The station was placed within the framework of Duga, under the auspices of Duga, which you were the director of, the information agency. That's the question. Isn't that what the municipal assembly did? They put it under you and Duga, D-u-g-a.

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That TV station organisationally speaking would be within that information company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the municipal assembly as part of their decision to adopt or to establish this television statement also indicated that its purpose -- what its purpose should be, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. Legal regulations stipulate what the decision on foundation on establishment is supposed to include. Inter alia such a decision should include what is called a programme concept, in a few sentences.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the programme concept was that it should be part of the unified mass media of Republika Srpska and that its purpose was to affirm the struggle of the Serbian people. That's what the municipal assembly indicated the purpose was, correct?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to see that document, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: P126, exhibit, please. Exhibit P126.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Article 4, number 48/93, 15 July 1993. Do you see Article 4, sir?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it says, "The programme of the Studio Samac television station shall be an integral part of the unified mass media of the Republika Srpska --

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct. That's not what it says here, or at least the interpretation I hear is not what is written here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why don't you read that paragraph, one sentence.

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Gladly. "The programme of TV Studio Samac is intended for the public information of citizens and for researching, disseminating information that pertains to questions that are of public importance." That is a sentence that has a content that is quite opposite to what we heard before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Read the next sentence, please. Or I'll read the next sentence.

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Paragraph or sentence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can the witness be directed to what he should read, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: It's the next sentence. It's the next sentence. It's the next paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Can he continue, then.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sure. Please do.

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you. "The programme of the TV station Studio Samac is an integral part of the unique information system of Republika Srpska, and it serves the purposes of affirming the struggle of the Serb people for its state and -- state sovereignty and economic and social prosperity."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note that they do not have any of these texts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. So when the reading is being done, please do it very slowly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it says: "The purpose shall be to affirm the struggle of the Serbian people," correct? Just as I said previously.

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You read the first paragraph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But that's what it says in the second paragraph, the struggle of the Serbian people. That's the purpose.

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, in 19 -- in December of 1994, the special rapporteur for the United Nations indicated different aspects of Serbian propaganda. One of them, common references to genocide. Another one, in battlefield, Serbian forces are almost always attacked and they defend themselves. Sir, isn't that what you were doing in Bosanski Samac, using that same type of propaganda that the special rapporteur to the United Nations complained about?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for this programme part relating to the establishment of the TV station, you could have seen just now that that is not what it says here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With regard to "Koridor" magazine, isn't that what you were doing in Bosanski Samac, just what the rapporteur of the United Nations complained about, those types of propaganda?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No? Sir, didn't it say that you shall include articles about genocide? Didn't it say that? Weren't those your directions from the assembly? We read those directions, sir. "'Koridor' shall contain features on the gathering of material evidence of war crimes and crimes of genocide committed against the Serbian population of the region." Isn't that one of the techniques that the special rapporteur has complained about? Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tell me one single text. Tell me of one single text that has dealt with that subject.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, the question is: The special rapporteur has indicated that Serbian genocide during the war included constant references -- I'm sorry, Serbian propaganda during the war included constant references to genocide committed against Bosnian Serbs. Now, sir, you were told -- I'm sorry, the magazine was told that its content shall contain features on gathering of material evidence of war crimes and crimes of genocide committed against the Serbian population of this region. Isn't that consistent with the special rapporteur's complaints on Serbian propaganda? That's what you were doing, just as the special rapporteur said.

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to know whether the special rapporteur bore in mind the "Koridor" newspaper and came to such conclusions. I don't think so. The "Koridor" was published in some 2 to 300 copies, and I think that the special rapporteur in his report did not have the "Koridor" in mind, nor do I have any knowledge to that effect, that he meant the "Koridor" magazine. If you have any knowledge in this respect, I would like to hear about it and then perhaps I could answer your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, he said that these press agencies were established by force precisely for the purpose of distorting information to serve the military and political objectives. That's what the special rapporteur said on December 14th, 1994, in paragraph 38. That was the Bosnian Serb press.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we object to the question put by the Prosecutor. It is the period of 1994 that is being discussed here, and the indictment refers to the period up to the end of 1993 as far as my client is concerned, at least, so it is not advisable to put these kind of questions related to a period that goes beyond the indictment. And after all, we had no opportunity of seeing this report. It was not admitted into evidence, and it was never exhibited.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I responded to his question. As this -- but as this Court knows, the special rapporteur was established by the United Nations in 1992. Their job or their function was to go out and determine whether human rights violations occurred from 1992 on, and that's what this rapporteur talks about, the various violations. And in the December 1994 edition, it talked about the use of propaganda during the war. It talked extensively about Serb propaganda, Muslim propaganda, and Croat propaganda. And the only reason I even brought that sentence up was I answered his question. He questioned me. Did it ever discuss? And I said, Yes, they discussed what exactly the Serb press was doing. They were distorting information to serve military and political objectives. If you'd like, I have a copy of it and I can confront him with it. Just like our expert witness in the first week of Prosecution, Mr. -- The expert Mr. Donia was confronted by a special rapporteur's report by Catharine Baen, which is Exhibit D2/2 for ID, and Catharine Baen did confront witnesses with that, even though that was not part of our case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Before I say anything, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My colleague the Prosecutor is now comparing this report in completely different contexts. Our colleague Ms. Baen mentioned this report in the context of expert witness Donia, related to visits to camps, and they were specifically mentioned in that report. If the Prosecutor is now invoking the report on propaganda, it has to be set very precisely. In which part does it pertain to propaganda. Because the period from 1991 to 1993 is a very broad one. And before that, the Prosecutor has to exactly specify the period in which the "Koridor" magazine was being published so that he could correlate the two. If this report refers to all years of the war, then the Prosecutor did not establish when the "Koridor" newspaper was established, and it is only then that he can correlate Mr. Mazowiecki's opinion to what the "Koridor" newspaper published. And I think that the wording from the Mazowiecki report is too broad based and therefore it cannot be put in such a way to this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, this witness has testified when he became the director of "Koridor" magazine. We --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I think, Mr. Weiner, the other important issue is that the report of the rapporteur, and even the Prosecution evidence, has not produced a single copy of the "Koridor." Is there any which we have -- where there is propaganda?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No. All I'm saying is he was ordered or the orders from --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes. I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, the order in part is okay. But as to whether or not the actual articles --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And all I want to say is the order he was giving as to the contents, those fall within the determinations of propaganda according to the special rapporteur. That's all I'm saying. His orders --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Nothing more than his orders basically, genocide that the Serbs always defend themselves and never attack, those fall within -- and I was going to show one more document and finish basically on this subject.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: If that is your explanation, then you can proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So my question was: The orders that you had from the assembly as to the content of that magazine that it shall include stories on genocide, that falls within -- or that's consistent with -- those directions are consistent with the special rapporteur's report that propaganda -- Serbian propaganda commonly used references to genocide.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. I don't believe that we heard anything here in the evidence that that was the order of the municipal assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, it was the decision of the municipal assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Decision is --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And it says "shall." It doesn't say "you may include. You can include." It says "you shall include." And if you look at the terminology in the exhibit, the word "shall" is there. And we all know the legal meaning of "shall." It's an order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic. I think the explanation is clear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the direction to include stories about crimes of genocide committed against the Serbian population, that is consistent with the report of the special rapporteur -- the comment of the special rapporteur that the Serbian propaganda included constant allegations to genocide.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't understand how the witness could answer that, unless he read the report of the special rapporteur of the UN, how could he answer that? He doesn't know what's in the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: He could answer that it does not. He could answer it does. Or he could answer "I don't know."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. I thought you had read, alia, that part of the conclusion of the special rapporteur.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Maybe you can repeat that so that he's directed as to what he's being asked to compare.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
