utterances.text: I'll read the full paragraph. May I give a copy to him so he can read the full paragraph instead of the phrase. I'll read the full paragraph and he can follow along with me. I have it in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Paragraph 39 from the special rapporteur's report of the 13th of December, 1994, "These media commonly refer to genocide committed against the Bosnian Serbs by Muslims and to Muslims as Mujahedins or Islamists, seeking to oppose Islam on Serbs. Killing Muslims is depicted virtually as a holy duty, the goal of which is to protect orthodoxy. In military reports from the battlefield, the Serbian forces are almost always attacked and then obliged to defend themselves, rarely initiating attacks themselves against the enemy. It is Muslim forces or the Ustasha, Croats, a reference to the fascist organisation active in Croatia during the Second World War who are always responsible for provocations." My question to you, sir: The directive that you received from the municipal assembly telling you that you shall gather material evidence of war crimes and crimes of genocide committed against the Serbian people, that direction to you is consistent with the complaint of the special rapporteur, is it not?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Quite simply, I cannot agree to fall into this trap which is called inverted logic. I simply cannot draw any parallel or see any link between what was done in the "Koridor" newspaper on the one hand and on the other hand what the special rapporteur wrote here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fine. Let's move on. Sir, the final thing I'd like you to look at is Exhibit 79. You testified about it on Friday, November 29th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see the document, sir?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you stated on Friday that this document was prepared for the press; isn't that correct? That's what you said on Friday.

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That document was prepared for the media.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you also stated that the date on it, April 17th, was incorrect.

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was incorrect or falsified or it was backdated, but the date was not correct. Now, do you know -- is that true? Is that correct, my statement? Is that a proper characterisation of your testimony, that the date was falsified, backdated, or it's incorrect?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It can be put that way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you know who prepared that document?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The professional staff of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, that document indicates that the Territorial Defence of the Serbian Municipality of Bosanski Samac was involved in a battle, correct?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It can be put that way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you weren't present on the early morning hours of the 17th in Bosanski Samac in the town to see that battle, correct?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not present in the early morning hours of the 17th of April in Samac so that I could see the battle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Nor were you present during the day, during the daytime hours, or at any time on the 17th of April in the town of Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not present.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, you didn't appear in Bosanski Samac until sometime on the 19th.

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the 19th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now -- so basically you never saw or you have no personal knowledge or any direct knowledge of what occurred in Bosanski Samac on the 17th or 18th. You have no direct knowledge or personal knowledge.

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already spoken about that. The first thing I saw was a number of uniforms of the ZNG, that is to say from the National Guards Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 17th or 18th, you didn't see anything. On the 17th --

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right. On the 17th and 18th, I did not see any of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this, as I said, indicates that the TO of the Serbian Municipality was involved in a battle here, and you said yes. Milan -- I'm sorry, Miroslav Tadic gave a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor on 26 March 1998. That's Exhibit P138, and the B/C/S version is P138 ter ID, which was admitted today.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: If the witness could see that, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It is not actually ID. If my colleague --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. 138 ter, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: P138 ter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to read how he describes the battle and its involvement with the 4th Detachment, which he also refers to as the Serbian TO. And let me find the page for you. Earlier Mr. Tadic describes the 4th Detachment as the local TO, or the local Serbian TO, on page 16. But let us --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Excuse me. Just which page for us?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. We're going to talk about page 24 in the English, and I believe it's page 33 -- page 33 in the B/C/S. "Q. But the 4th was involved in the takeover on the 17th of April; isn't it true?" Answer by Mr. Tadic: "No. "Q. Who managed the takeover of the town of Bosanski Samac then if the 4th Detachment was not involved? "A. It was not a problem to take over Bosanski Samac. There was the Serbian police, some trained police -- I'm sorry, some trained people, and half an hour they took over Bosanski Samac without any shots being fired, without shelling, without the war. "Q. There was no resistance offered by the non-Serbs? "A. Mostly no resistance. Perhaps partly some, but not significant. "Q. So if there was no fighting going on and there was no resistance, what was the need to take over the town in the first place? "A. Now, this is more of kind of a political question, and the reason for this takeover was that in order to prevent an inter-ethnic conflict, because there was some information given that there was some indications as well as that there would be an inter-ethnic conflict was waiting to happen. So this was done in order to prevent it. So this takeover happened, if we can call it, conditionally speaking." As you note, he doesn't say anything about an involvement of a Serbian TO. In fact, the group he describes as the Serbian TO, the 4th Detachment, he says was not involved. Isn't that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 17th and the 18th I was not an eyewitness. But still, I cannot say that I was hibernating at the time because the sound of artillery fire --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, the question --

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- reached me in Kruskovo Polje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, once again the question is: Miroslav Tadic doesn't say anything about the involvement of a Serbian TO. In fact, the group he describes as the Serbian TO, the 4th Detachment, he says was not involved. Isn't that correct, sir? That's the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe that this question is not quite appropriate. First, looking through the interview of Mr. Miroslav Tadic, there is no one single place where he said 4th Detachment was actually Serbian TO. He was talking about 4th Detachment. Whether he thought that it is the Serbian TO or something else, I don't believe it's fair to ask this witness to comment something that it is not even clear to the Prosecution or to us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner, any response?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Page 16.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But is the 4th Detachment and TO the same thing?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Page 16 he calls it the same thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So my question again -- my question again, sir: Miroslav Tadic doesn't say anything about the involvement of a Serbian TO. In fact, the group he describes as the Serbian TO, the 4th Detachment, he says was not involved. Is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can answer this question once the term "some people trained there" is explained to me. That's the term that I did not understand. The first part of it, "Trained people," can indicate people wearing uniforms, but it can also indicate people that had gone through some military training. This is why this term is unclear to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I also do not understand to whom these trained people belonged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Those were members of the special battalion, locals that were trained in Serbia. But getting back to the question. The question, sir, again, is -- and it's a simple question -- Miroslav Tadic doesn't say anything about the involvement of a Serbian TO. In fact, the group he describes as a Serbian TO, the 4th Detachment, he says was not involved. Is that correct, sir? Is that a correct reading of that document?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot comprehend that and come to that conclusion based on what I had heard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I'm not asking you what you've heard and comparing that to what you've heard. I'm asking you what Miroslav Tadic states in his -- indicates in his statement. In that statement that you have in front of you, he does not indicate that the Serbian TO or the 4th Detachment, whatever you would like to call it, was involved in a takeover; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on this statement of Miroslav Tadic, I cannot come to that conclusion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that statement of Miroslav Tadic does not indicate that the Serbian TO and the 4th Detachment was not involved in the takeover. That statement of Miroslav Tadic does not indicate that. Is that what you're saying, sir?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I can see on the basis of the statement of Miroslav Tadic is that he himself was not quite clear about the identity of those trained and uniformed people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Despite my willingness, I'm unable to do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, he specifically says the 4th Detachment, which he describes as the Serbian TO, was not involved in the takeover. Is that what he says? If you'd like, I'll read it to you again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, Mr. Weiner. I think we've belaboured the point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, Mr. Simo Zaric has also given a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor on April 2nd, 1998, Exhibit P141.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: We'd like to hand in at this time the ter document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we have the number, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Page 7 in the English.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Exhibit P141 ter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And this is the interview by Mr. Simo Zaric of the 2nd April 1998.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]. "Q. I'm sorry. I have missed this along the way -- that's the beginning of the question. When was it that Nikolic received this call from Simic informing him that they had made the decision to take over? Do you see that question? Do you see that question on yours?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could we have a page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Page 7 in the English.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see it, sir?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Weiner. On what page in the ter document?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: 12 on the ter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can see it at the top.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Answer by Mr. Zaric, by the defendant Zaric: "A. And Nikolic told us that he had received a call from Blagoje Simic on the 16th after midnight - so it was actually the 17th - very, very early in the morning -- in the night telling him that the Crisis Staff had decided to take over the town of Samac, that it would then become the Serbian Municipality of Samac, that there were Serbian police and units were taking over all the vital buildings and objects in the town. Now, I'd like to say something, that the official authorities in the town, whenever during the war, when the anniversary would come up on this date, the 16th of April, they would celebrate and look upon it as an anniversary of liberation. That is the word they used to express it. And they said it was liberation carried out by the Serbian police and Serbian volunteers, but they never even mentioned the 4th Detachment." Is that what it says? Is that what it says, sir?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question. What is your question to me? And as to what you have just read out --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did I read that out correctly, sir?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You did, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there anything in that statement from the defendant Simo Zaric indicating that the Serbian TO was involved in a battle on April 17th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only thing I can say is that there are a few incorrect bits here in this text. The first one is that Blagoje Simic was not a JNA officer. He was not able to issue orders to any military formations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It doesn't -- it does not say that Blagoje Simic was a JNA officer. It says he issued those orders on behalf of the Crisis Staff on the 16th of April -- or actually, on the 17th of April, in the early, early morning hours, it says.

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Blagoje Simic could not have issued orders to soldiers of the JNA or to the Territorial Defence or any other military formation. This is why this passage is not clear to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, does it indicate that the Serbian TO was involved in a battle on April 17th, 1992? We'll get back to Blagoje Simic.

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see that in this first paragraph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, let's go back to Exhibit 79, P79, sir. That exhibit, the first two paragraphs talk about a battle. Is there anything in that exhibit, in that one-page exhibit, indicating that a pre-emptive strike was used to take over the town of Bosanski Samac? Is that listed anywhere on P79? We're back at P79, the piece -- the exhibit that was sent to the press. Is there anywhere in that exhibit or statement that a pre-emptive strike was used to take over the town of Bosanski Samac? Does it say that anywhere on that page?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It doesn't say here "in order to take over power" in the second paragraph. Rather, it says here that these forces acted pre-emptively in order to stop the attack, to prevent the attack, or the incursion of the Army of the Republic of Croatia and paramilitary formations into Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, it says that in the first paragraph, "Units from Croatia, along with Green Berets and units of the so-called Territorial Defence tried to occupy the town." Does it state anywhere that a pre-emptive strike was taken to take over the town? Does it say that anywhere, a pre-emptive strike was utilised to take over that town?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The mere fact that the forces from the Croatian territory came there. That's what it means.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, that's not my question. Does it state that a pre-emptive strike was used to take over the town?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It doesn't say here "in order to take over the power," but rather, "in order to prevent the incursion of the formations from the --"

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are the words "a pre-emptive strike was used to take over the town" in that letter?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In what letter? I'm sorry, I am -- it's not clear to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- Does it use the words "a pre-emptive strike was utilised to take over the town"?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, these words are not used there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Does it state that Serbian police and volunteers from Serbia were involved in a battle to take over the town? Does it say that?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. And I would like somebody to convince me in that by quoting something that would prove that it was the volunteers from Serbia and some other forces involved in it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, we just quoted statements from two of the co-defendants in the case. Let's move on to the next question. Does it state that there was very little resistance from the non-Serbs? Does it state that in the letter which you used to send to the press -- in the document that you sent to the press, that there was very little resistance from the non-Serb population?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It doesn't say that. It contains a general definition to the effect that last night paramilitary formations attempted to occupy the territory of Samac municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I can read that too. All my question is: Does it state that there was very little resistance from the non-Serb population? That's all.

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no specific term here regarding the resistance. Unless you interpret the term "occupy," then one can assume that a significant force needs to exist in order to accomplish that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We're not going to assume. We're not going to try and interpret. We're just looking at the words. Finally, is there any indication, is there any statement in that document that Blagoje Simic, on behalf of the Crisis Staff, called Nikolic and asked him to take over the town?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of this document, I cannot conclude something of that nature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, if those things happened as stated by Mr. Tadic and Mr. Zaric and these first two paragraphs in this document are false, isn't it true that this letter is nothing more than a piece of propaganda?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You have used the word "if" several times. And then on the basis of your own thesis, you reached a conclusion. In logic, this is called inverted logic. That's what I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you to accept those two hypotheticals, that what Zaric and Tadic said was true. There was no Serbian TO involved in the battle.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Objection. Calling for speculation. Pure speculation, Your Honour. It's even a part of his question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is the information director or however you want to call it, the information chief of the Crisis Staff. He's responsible for meeting with the public. If these two paragraphs are false, he can answer whether or not this is just all propaganda.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Because the interviews -- the passages -- the relevant passages of the interviews have been read to the witness, so he can compare that with what the content of the document he is looking at are talking about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So my question to you, sir: If those first two paragraphs are false and you weren't there -- you've admitted you weren't there for the battle -- if those first two paragraphs of the statement are false and the statements from Tadic and Zaric are true, indicating those two paragraphs are false, isn't that document nothing more than a piece of propaganda that was given to the press?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document cannot be pure propaganda, nor can it be said that it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So even if it's false, even if those first two paragraphs are false, that's not propaganda, that document. Putting out false information to the press, that's not propaganda, sir?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: False information was not spread, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If those two paragraphs are false, sir, isn't that document a piece of propaganda?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be quite frank, I'm not clear on what is incorrect now. Is it what was stated by Mr. Tadic and Zaric, or is it these two paragraphs contained in this proclamation? If you are referring to the paragraphs in the proclamation, then they are correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, if those first two paragraphs are false -- if those first two paragraphs are false, isn't this document consistent with paragraph 39 of the special rapporteur's report, where he states -- where he talks about Serbian propaganda. "In military reports from the battlefield, the Serbian forces are almost always attacked and then obliged to defend themselves, rarely initiating attacks themselves against the enemy." If those first two paragraphs are false, isn't that exactly what the special rapporteur for the United Nations mentioned in his complaints about Serbian propaganda?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But these very paragraphs are correct, and I will take the liberty of giving you my impression regarding this and tell you that this reminds me of a famous saying by Richelieu and saying, "Give me an innocent sentence and I will turn it into something else."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You weren't there. You can't say what happened. You've only received information. My question is again: If those two paragraph that is the Crisis Staff sent to the press are false, if those two paragraphs are false, isn't that falsity consistent with the complaint of the special prosecutor as to Serbian propaganda, where the special rapporteur states -- sorry, not the special prosecutor -- the special rapporteur states, "In military reports from the battlefield, the Serbian forces are almost always attacked and then obliged to defend themselves, rarely initiating attacks themselves against the enemy." Isn't that consistent with the special rapporteur's report, that those two paragraphs are false, yes or no.

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no information to the effect that the special rapporteur had in mind either this proclamation or anything else that took place in Samac in terms of information spread there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For three full day it is artillery shelled --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's not the question. The question is: Assuming those two paragraphs are false, isn't that consistent with the special rapporteur's complaint about Serbian propaganda where, . "Military reports from the battlefield, the Serbian forces are almost always attacked and then obliged to defend themselves, rarely initiating attacks themselves against the enemy." That's at paragraph 39 which was read to you and which you saw. Assuming those two paragraphs are false, isn't that consistent with the special rapporteur's report?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never base my conclusions on incorrect assumptions. I always base them on what I know to be true. Therefore, I wouldn't like to go into speculations regarding untruths.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I also wouldn't like to link that with the report --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner -- Mr. Weiner, I think we'll go on. You won't get the answer you want.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: It's obvious. Thank you. No further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Re-examination, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour. Re-examined by Mr. Pantelic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's go back to facts, because we have dealt with a lot of assumptions here. First question: Were there any Croat attacks from mid-July 1992 -- mid April, sorry, 1992?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were attacks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Second question: Were there SDA and HDZ elements in Samac which were militarily organised?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The Croatian Democratic Union had the HVO and the SDA had the Green Berets as armed formations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is the bridge towards Prud as part of Samac municipality, as part of the municipality of Samac, was it closed between the 20 -- the April 1992 and May 1992?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Croat armed forces and other armed persons were on that bridge long before that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any shelling --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Allow the answer to the witness to be completed in the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Your question was: Were there any shelling -- and then you're supposed to continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Was there any shelling of Samac by the Croat army?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were Serbs in Odzak detained in April and May 1992?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In Odzak there were about 3500 to 4000 detained Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Samac up to July 1992 completely militarily encircled? Was it surrounded by the army?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: That's outside the scope of cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It's very inside the scope.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, I'll allow the question because --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It's very inside the scope.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The question will be allowed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And these are also very leading questions. He can ask what happened, when things happened. But he's saying, Did this -- Didn't this in fact happen? Didn't this in fact happen? Just yes and no answers, they're also very leading.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, we already have that in our evidence during the examination of this witness. You can find in his examination-in-chief all these answers. So it's an indisputable fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You still can't lead. He still can't lead, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I would like to wind up, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What you want is to reaffirm what the witness said earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. You can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And now it's my final question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Simic, are these facts or propaganda, all these questions that I've just asked you?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are pure facts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Simic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: -- P12 -- sorry, it's 125, I believe. Yes. P125. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Simic, go to page 34 of this Official Gazette number 2, dated 8 August 1994.

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I may have the usher's assistance, please, with finding the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: What page in the English, counsel?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, this is the decision that -- it was discussed during the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No, I know. Just what page are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Frankly -- oh, it's really a mess here because it was -- number 2. Because my version here is completely regular, and I really don't know what is the -- yes. Yes. It's page 34 -- ERN number is 00456707 B/C/S version. And accordingly, the English version is -- should be page 11. Actually, this is a decision on the founding of the "Koridor" magazine.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Page 11.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Simic, can you please explain to me this act. What kind of an act is that?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the decision on the foundation of "Koridor" magazine, which was passed by the Municipal Assembly of the Municipality of Samac at its session on the 17th of April, 1993, in keeping with the legal regulations which envisage the items that are contained in the document, i.e., in the founding act.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Is that an order?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not an order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this -- was this decision unnecessary? Did it have to be passed in order to register a company? So is this an act to incept a company?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: An inception act is mandatory as per the regulations of the municipal assembly so as to put this magazine within the legal system.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Next question: Please look carefully at Articles 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, and 8. Can you please look at these articles very carefully.

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We are still talking about the decision to found "Koridor" magazine. Have you looked at it?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, can you please find this decision -- or try to find in this decision wherever you can the future, the grammar -- the grammatical future form. In the decision that you have in front of you, can you find anywhere future tense, anywhere where it says "it shall be"? Is there the grammatical future form, the shell form in this decision?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there is no shell and there is no imperative in this decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me. I'd like to perhaps ask the witness to read out the sentence in the B/C/S that Mr. Weiner read out in English where the word "shall" was used and then Mr. Weiner talked about the mandatory nature therefore. So now we hear the witness saying there's no "shall" in the B/C/S text, and I think we clearly want this cleared up.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour. Gladly. That's the point. Because all this big story was just because of the inconsistency in the translation. But I will clarify that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Simic, can you please read to begin with paragraph 2, Article 4 -- Article 4, the paragraph begins with the word "magazine."

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "This magazine will be published twice a month" -- "the magazine shall be published twice a month."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you read it again because we have problems with the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: This document, P125, has been translated by the ICTY, and they have used the word "shall" eight times. And I think if there's an issue as to whether or not the word "shall" is in this, I think the translators should read this, because they've already published in document indicating the word "shall" appears eight times in those eight articles. That's --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And in the B/C/S version --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: This is the ICTY version.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: -- the word "shall" -- we don't have any such form. So that's always a problem, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, that's not the point. We always accept the official translation, that's all. So there's no argument about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I just want to reiterate position that it was not in a form of order and there is no imperative form here in this original version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me. Excuse me. Mr. Pantelic, I'm just wondering why if your position is -- your submission is that there's an inconsistency between the B/C/S and the English and we've got "shall" in the English eight times and not at all or whatever in the B/C/S, why -- why didn't you object to the translation when the Prosecution originally introduced it?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Because, Your Honour, I was of the opinion that I will clarify that during the re-examination. Simply as that. I didn't want to interrupt the proceedings during the cross-examination of my learned friend. So it was -- arose just during the cross-examination, this theory -- Prosecution theory that it's an order, that this form is in future, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well then. Mr. Simic --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, once again, this document has been translated by the ICTY, not our office. And if someone is going to read out -- I miscounted, because I've counted quickly. It's ten times in eight paragraph it is the word "shall." This document was tendered on the 1st of June. No one has objected to this document up to this point. If someone should read it out, can they -- can we have the translators read it out, especially they --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We are not going to deal with all that and waste time. Each party is presenting its case according to its own understanding. And then the Trial Chamber will be able to decide on what is and what is not after tall evidence has been adduced. So the parties should be concerned with the substance of the case rather than this grammatical problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Look at the first paragraph of Article 4. And can you please read it.

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "'Koridor' is the magazine of the people in Posavina and is intended for the information of citizens, for the research, collection, and dissemination of information and idea relative to the issues of public significance."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please comment on this paragraph. What is the meaning of this paragraph?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The meaning of this paragraph is that "Koridor" magazine informed citizens regardless of their social or ethnical or any other affiliation on all the issues of any importance to them. So this is the meaning of this paragraph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any authorities in the municipality have the right or could they influence the editorial policy of "Koridor" magazine?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The editorial policy of any media, including the printed media, is regulated by law and the person responsible before the law is the editor-in-chief. And none of the politicians could interfere with that because that was punishable by law.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did it ever happen in Samac that any political leaders influenced the content of "Koridor" magazine, i.e., what should be published in it?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No politicians ever influenced the editorial policy of that magazine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Mr. Blagoje Simic ever influence the type of articles that was to be published or the editorial policy of "Koridor"?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Blagoje Simic did not interfere in the editorial policy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This decision that you've been reading now, is that -- was that authored by Blagoje Simic or was it voted in favour of by the councilmen at the session of the assembly of the municipality?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: He can ask who put this policy together. He can ask when was it put together. Once again, these are very leading questions. I've let it go two or three. But it's just one after another. These are statements. Counsel is testifying at this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But we have to be focussed on certain issues, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. You should avoid leading questions. But on the other hand, these are matter which have already been gone through by the witness and are on record as to the procedures on how the Crisis Staff or the assembly operated.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay. Let me check.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Again, I'm going to ask you what you know about the way in which this decision was passed at the session of the Municipal Assembly of Samac on the 17th of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This decision was passed at the regular session of the Municipal Assembly of Samac where there were 50 assemblymen present.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Once again, an interpretation. In paragraph 1, Article 4, this notion of free research, how do you understand that? Could you interpret it for me.

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Journalists were to be given -- or rather, this meant that journalists were supposed to work more on what is called investigative journalism.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. The Prosecutor during the cross-examination put a question to you and quoted Simo Zaric to you. Was he a member of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Simo Zaric was not a member of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any idea why he made comments with regard to the activities of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot know why he made such comments, unless it has something to do with his service.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the Prosecutor asked you questions, you mentioned an event that occurred before you went to the assembly in May 1992. You said that it was something that was truly impressive, and he didn't want to ask you any more about this. So what was this impressive event that took place before you went to the municipal assembly then?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was very impressive from the point of view of my own experience because then I entered the municipal assembly under a cannonade of shells, and I found there the staff members of the assembly in the basement. They were very frightened. So that is this experience I had. Otherwise, I did not go. On other occasions, I did not go to the municipal assembly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where is the municipal assembly building?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The municipal assembly building is in the main street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about its other side? Where does that face?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Its other side faces an apartment building and the building of the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Let's clarify this. One side faces the street. Where does the other side opposite that face?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see. The other side faces the Sava -- or rather, the border with Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was across the Sava River, apart from the fact that it was the border?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Across the Sava River were the Croat forces. And during the first days of war a tank was operating from there, and that could be seen with the naked eye.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what the distance is between this Samac building and the other side, the Croat side in metres tentatively?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, perhaps 600 to 700 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is a pretty broad river, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a part -- well, it is an area that is not populated. But from time to time water would come there, but usually it would withdraw. So when I said 600 to 700 metres, I mean up to the border. I mean the other bank of the river. That is where the Croatian border is, and that includes the width of the river.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand. Since you were involved in the field of information, can you tell us what you know about the number of journalists and crews of journalists between April and June and how often did this take place.

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Different teams and crews of journalists came in, both from home and abroad. And I remember that a TV crew - I think it was from England - produced a programme about the rape of women. Also, they made another programme -- or rather, they filmed the funeral of a Serb fighter. Unfortunately later it was shown on Croatian TV as the funeral of a Muslim soldier, and that is not something that is unknown. There is a video cassette of that particular event, and the wife of the killed fighter has it, and his last name was Drinic. He had a Masters of Science degree in machine building.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Is this relevant to our case?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question is the following: These journalists who came between April and July, these journalists from home and abroad, did they have free access to all facilities all over town? Did they manage to visit everywhere and write about anything they wished to write about?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for the civilian part, they had access to all the facilities that have to do with these particular authorities. But as regards the police and the military, as far as I know, special permits were required, permits issued by commander, persons who were in commanding positions, that is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about journalists who were coming to Samac and their free movement about town? Were they allowed to move about town freely?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Journalists who came to Samac could move about freely, about town, that is, and I personally went with some of these crews and journalists through town. I remember when the Croatian artillery was firing I asked, "Can you hear the artillery? Do you know where this is coming from? Do you know where this artillery gunfire is coming from?"

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could these journalists from home and abroad talk unhindered to the population of Samac in the period between April and July 1992 and further on in the years to come?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Which population is he talking about? Is he talking about the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Since he hasn't indicated whether or not they visited prisons, I take it he's talking about the ordinary population.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The free -- those who were free and residents in the town of Samac.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Journalists and journalist crews could talk to ordinary citizens of Samac, and they did talk to them. In these talks, I was an eyewitness too.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If journalists wanted to talk to prisoners, then who could give them a permit for that? Which service would give them a permit for doing that?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This permit would have to be issued to them by one of the chiefs of police or perhaps if they went to the front line, they should get such a permit from army commanders.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: In your position as the Crisis Staff information man, when you were talking to these journalists from home and abroad, do you know whether any of them were actually granted a permit by the chief of police or the military? And particularly with regard to the chief of police to go and see the persons detained in the -- the SUP and later on in the elementary school and so on. If you could assist, that would be very good.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know about one case, when the military -- or rather, the military authorities gave a permit to journalists from a foreign journalist crew to tour a particular area that they were interested in. However, sometimes journalists would also take their own routes, so to speak, apart from the information service of the Crisis Staff. So I cannot really know about everybody.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: So to your knowledge, you only know of one journalist who was given a permit by the military. What about the chief of police, Mr. Todorovic? Did he issue any permits to journalists who maybe then came in and told you that they had seen prisoners or detainees?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Some journalists said that they had seen prisoners and that they had been to see Mr. Todorovic. But I did not see these papers of theirs, or rather, this permit, and I don't know whether this was regulated verbally or whether there was an official permit that was issued.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One more question before the break to conclude this subject. Was there a censorship service at the level of the municipality of Samac, vis-a-vis journalists who came to do their jobs? Were their reports censored or could they publish them freely?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course they would not agree to any kind of censorship and of course they freely published whatever they saw, heard, found out. No one imposed any kind of censorship upon them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I think it's time for our break, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We shall rise and continue at 14.30 hours. --- Luncheon recess taken at 1.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic. Re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour. Thank you, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Simic, before the break, we completed the topic regarding the visit of journalists, and now I would like to turn to another topic which was covered during the cross-examination. I'm referring now to the document -- to the information that you commented.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: -- Exhibit P127.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Sorry. Sorry. My mic was off.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you please interpret and translate -- and explain to the Trial Chamber if you know. In the upper left corner, there is written "Pov Broj." And what do you know about this term used on documents?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have it on my document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It should be in the upper left corner.

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It says here "Pov Broj."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What can you tell us? What does this mean, based on what you know?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It means, as in all other documents of that nature, this is a strictly confidential document, which means it is intended only for a narrow circle of people that had to be familiarised with the subject matter of this text.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. So that means that was an internal document of a military unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'd object again. Counsel is testifying here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic. No leading questions, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, this document, as you see it in front of you, can you based on this document conclude that it was intended for public use? You have seen a lot of documents in your career.

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since this is a strictly confidential document, it means intended only to be used by the highest officials, commanders of the 2nd Posavina Infantry Brigade. This document was not available to the public in general at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In view of the competencies of military commanders when it comes to appointment of military commanders, which is something covered during cross-examination, I would like to ask you the following: Do you know who Colonel Dencic is?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Colonel Dencic was commander of East Bosnia Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that military formation superior to 2nd Posavina Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is superior military command. The 2nd Posavina Infantry Brigade was subordinated to the East Bosnia Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you personally know what was the role of Colonel Dencic in removal from office and appointment of military commanders who were subordinated to him? If you know, please.

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not difficult to know that. Colonel Dencic was authorised to appoint people to lower command posts, including brigade commanders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know anything about the appointment of the commander of the 2nd Posavina Brigade from June to August 1992?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During that period of time, commanders of 2nd Posavina Infantry Brigade were appointed by Commander Dencic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please tell us, during the term of the War Presidency, meaning from the second half of July 1992 until the regular session of the municipal assembly was convened, who was the commander of the 2nd Posavina Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the time period.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will. The time period was the one during the term of War Presidency, meaning from late July 1992 until the first session of the regular municipal assembly. If you know, who was the commander of the 2nd Posavina Brigade during that time?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of the 2nd Posavina Infantry Brigade was Major, and later Lieutenant Colonel and Colonel, Mile Beronja.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who appointed officer Beronja to commander of 2nd Posavina Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was appointed by the commander of the East Bosnia Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Prior to July 1992, starting from mid-May 1992, when you said that the JNA left the area. So this is the period that we're interested in. Who was commander of the 2nd Posavina Brigade then?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were two commanders as far as I can remember. Dragan Djordjevic and Srecko Radovanovic. But I couldn't give you the temporal framework.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Can you tell us who appointed the two of them commanders of the 2nd Posavina Brigade then.

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The two of them were appointed by the commander who was in charge of that, commander of East Bosnia Corps, Colonel Dencic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since you gave quite detailed answers regarding the document that is in front of you now, I wouldn't like to go back to certain motives and so on. You've already explained that quite well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'd object to that question. The editorial section on he gave detailed answers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: To the -- I'd object to that. That's just -- that's argumentative. Move to strike that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask you: According to your knowledge, what were the motives for having this document appear in public?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already answered that question partially. This document probably appeared in public as an instrument of political struggle between certain groupations within between military structures. There also could have been a war between various intelligence services.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: The wording used in the language: "This document probably appeared," and then he later said, "There also could have been a war." Those are both answers or statements indicating speculation, as opposed to a statement indicating facts of what exactly occurred. I move to strike as nothing more than speculation based on the wording he used in his answers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Pantelic, you understand the objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. It's okay, Your Honour. I will --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I think the witness should give answers which are certain. Either he knows or he doesn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: My question was very clear, according to your knowledge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will repeat the question. We're now interested in what you personally know. You were in Samac at that time. You know the circumstances surrounding this. Now, please tell us, what do you personally know about the fate of this document or its use? What do you personally know?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I know is that military organs always tried to impose some kind of a domination over the civilian organs, civilian authorities. This is what I know about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you now referring to the territory of Samac municipality during the relevant period of time?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm now referring to the territory of Samac municipality only partially, because this phenomenon was present in other areas as well, where there were military and civilian authorities. I've already said that this culminated during the incident called September 1993. This conflict persisted throughout the war, the conflict between military and civilian authorities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you this now: Please tell the Trial Chamber what happened in late 1992 in the premises of the heating plant when this document was created. Did somebody come to visit you there? What were the circumstances? Please tell the Trial Chamber about this.

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At that time two men came to visit me -- or rather, they called me from the Crisis Staff premises. These two men before Lazar Stanisic, a member of the military police, and the second one was Fadil Topcagic, a soldier. Mr. Lazar Stanisic was also an assemblyman in the municipal assembly. He informed me that in the village of Slatina a session of Samac Municipal Assembly was scheduled to be held. I asked him to show me notice and summons to attend it; however, he had nothing of the sort on him and he simply told me that I was being invited to attend by the Serb people. Then I asked him that scheduling and convening of the sessions of the municipal assembly are conducted according to a very established procedure; namely, that the sessions were convened by the leadership of the assembly, or rather, its president and that according to the statute a session may be also convened by the assemblymen of the assembly providing that they have ten signatures collected, ten people in favour of convening the session. There were no such signatures there, nor was there any notice to attend signed by the president of the assembly. As I later heard, this session was held unlawfully, without a quorum, in Slatina, in the village of Gornja Slatina. Again, as I heard later, some assemblymen attended the session; however, they didn't have quorum and the session could not be held. Some officers from the 2nd Posavina Infantry Brigade were present as well. That was one of the attempts to -- of the military authorities to interfere in the work of civilian authorities. This is what I personally know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could we have, please, Exhibit D29/4, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Have you ever seen this document before? If you have, can you tell us something about it.

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have seen this document. This is an interim issue of the bulletin which explains precisely the things that I have just been talking about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the regular session of the assembly convened after these events?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was. After that - that is, somewhat later - a session of the municipal assembly was convened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it convened in keeping with the regulations, or was it convened based on some other initiatives?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This session of the municipal assembly was convened in keeping with the statute of the Samac Municipal Assembly, so it was legally convened, based on regulations.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Usher. You can take the document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's move on to a different topic. The Prosecution asked you about some court documents, most specifically a statement given by Blagoje Simic in the proceedings before that court. Do you have any personal knowledge or do you remember when that statement was given before the investigative judge in Banja Luka? Can you remember? Or maybe we can put the document in front of you.

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd rather have the document in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It's -- just a minute. We have the number here. It's P116, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the left upper corner of this document it says the date. Can you read it, please.

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 14 December 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the middle of the document, you will see the place where the statement was given. Can you please read it.

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Military court in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the middle towards the bottom, it is in the premises of the heating factory in Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In December 1992, what municipal institution --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, what it states is it was taken before a military judge in the court in Banja Luka. Down towards the lower part of the page, it says the interview was conducted on the premises of the Samac heating plant. It's misrepresenting the document and the evidence here, or it's just mistaken.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Maybe it's your misunderstanding, my dear friend. I can clarify you. The institution is military court in Banja Luka, but the testimony was made in the premises of heating plant in Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: That's what I'm saying. However, what you stated here is -- let's go back. The place where the statement was given, and he's testified "military court in Banja Luka." And you directed him to that, right -- look at the transcript. 81, 9 -- 81, 6 through 11. You're directing him to give evidence that's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. My meaning was here, I believe. My meaning was the institution which was deployed in Samac. But no problem. In my next question I was -- I was -- I was quite precise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Simic, which municipal institution or which body had its seat or headquarters in the heating plant in Samac?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was at the time the War Presidency, which was headquartered in the heating plant in Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, then. When you analyse the information that you have just discussed and when you analyse the events surrounding that information and knowing that these proceedings were organised by the military prosecution or judiciary, so what conclusions can you arrive at and what are your personal -- your personal knowledge about these three events?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: He's asking him some sort of conclusion, which I'm not certain what it is, to speculate or a legal conclusion or -- it's not clear what --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It's his personal knowledge of the chain of the events with regard to the letter of 13 signatories, with regard to the issue of proceedings before the investigating judge in the military court, and with regard to the attempt to organise some kind of plenary session of the municipal assembly, et cetera. These three basic events, what his personal knowledge about all these events in December 1992. That's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I don't want him to speculate on legal grounds or whatever.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: He can ask for his personal knowledge on various events, but that's not what the question was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well. Now he has explained that he's asking the witness about his personal knowledge. So we'll go by that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: His personal knowledge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So your personal knowledge -- in order for us to speed up the procedure, we were talking about the document signed by the 13 signatories about the proceedings which were conducted before that court and you also told us about the initiative to convene a session of the assembly. So all that took place simultaneously. What is your personal knowledge of the relationship between -- among these three events, if you have any personal knowledge?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All of these events are interrelated. And it was the time when strong pressure came from military circles upon the organs of the civilian authorities, and that resulted in an illegal session of the assembly being convened. At the moment when the corridor was closed, the president of the War Presidency, Dr. Blagoje Simic, for two or three days had to go into hiding and his security men told me that some men in uniform had come and asked about him and also that he had gone away and never told anybody his address. So there was a strong pressure on the president of the War Presidency. I didn't know the cause of these pressures, but they were very obvious, very visible, and his security personnel knew all that very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What period are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the period of time when the corridor was closed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please state the month and the year for the record, if you can remember that. First the year.

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in 1992; I'm sure of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please specify the period.

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the second half of that year. It was the summer of that year, July or August maybe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were explaining to the Prosecutor that you were also arrested by the military organs and that you were detained for a period of time. In November or December 1992, when all of these things happened, were you personally afraid as a member of the Crisis Staff of the military organs? What was your attitude towards the military organs at the time? Did you have -- did you experience any personal fear?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not experience any personal fear of the military judiciary, but I was constantly afraid of the members of the army and of their actions. Very often these people did not perform their duties within the scope of their authority. More often than not they would exceed their authorities, and that was the cause of the constant fear, the fear of such actions by the military circles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Prosecutor also asked you a series of questions relative to the position of the Serbian Municipality of Bosanski Samac, that is, Pelagicevo, which was being founded at the time. Do you know when the Serbian Municipality of Bosanski Samac and Pelagicevo was established?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That municipality -- and I believe that I've said that already -- according to my knowledge was established in February.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of what year?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does the Municipality of Samac still exist? Does it function?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it still exists and it functions within the entity of the Republika Srpska and the State of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Samac -- Municipality Samac is part of the entity and known as Republika Srpska. But there is also the Croatian Municipality of Samac, which is located, i.e., its centre is in Domaljevac, which is a village which used to belong to Samac municipality in the past.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does Republika Srpska represent? Is that one of the entities and an entity of what?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Republika Srpska is one of the entities of the State of Bosnia and Herzegovina, according to the Dayton Accords.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is exactly what I wanted to ask you. When were the Dayton Accords signed?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Dayton Accords were --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic. Where are we going? You're wasting time?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: My clarification, Your Honour, is with regard to the fact that Municipality of Samac is a legitimate part of Republika Srpska, which is a legitimate part of Bosnia-Herzegovina internationally recognised.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. But -- so what's the point? Because that has been given in evidence and the Trial Chamber takes judicial notice of what the status of the variant entities are. You're wasting time, and this means that you're through with your re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Only three more questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well. You ask the three questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Prosecutor asked you about certain plans which were published in the Official Gazette of Samac Municipality. Do you have any personal knowledge of any plans which were published in the Official Gazette of Samac Municipality?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Next question: The Prosecutor also asked you to explain something about the people who were awarded with the St. Vitus award. My question is: What body proposed the persons with military ranks for this award?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some military bodies and the organisation of fighters. There was something called the Association of Veterans of Samac Municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: According to your information, did military organs undertake any measures to arrest and to conduct proceedings against Lugar as the perpetrator of crimes in Crkvina?

utterances.speaker: SIMEON SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether any measures were taken either by the Army of Republika Srpska or JNA in order to process this crime.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Simic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I've finished with my re-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you, Mr. Simic, for giving evidence to the Trial Chamber. You are now through, and you can go.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Before we start the next witness, the Trial Chamber has a ruling on the application for the certificate. And the ruling is going to be given orally. The Trial Chamber is seized of the joint Defence requests for Rule 73 certification filed by the Defence of all three accused on 14th November. The Prosecution has not responded to the joint requests. Having considered the submission of the Defence on this matter, the Trial Chamber hereby renders its decision on the joint request. The Trial Chamber recalls that the basis for the rejection of the expert opinion of Colonel Ostoja Barisici [phoen] was that: One, it purports to make conclusions which are the duty of this Trial Chamber to draw in connection with certain major issues in this case; Second, that the said expert opinion lends support to the argument of tu quoque and was therefore irrelevant. And three, that the procedure contemplated under Rule 94 bis does not affect the general power of the Trial Chamber to exclude evidence under Rule 89 of the Rules. The Trial Chamber thus rejected the evidence as being of no assistance in the performance of its task. In the joint request, the Defence submits that the intent to establish via the said expert opinion the basic principles of subordination within the JNA in order to explain what the actual positions of the accused, namely, Miroslav Tadic and Simo Zaric were. This does not address the basis upon which the Trial Chamber rejected the evidence. The Trial Chamber is of the view that this submission involves establishing a situation of fact, which may be more suitably done through the calling of fact witnesses. In this regard, the Trial Chamber notes that the Defence of Simo Zaric and of Miroslav Tadic propose to call witnesses who will be giving evidence on this matter. Under Rule 73(B) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, the Trial Chamber may grant a certificate provided that, one, the impugned decision involves an issue that would significantly affect the fair and expeditious conduct of the proceedings or the outcome of the trial. And two, the Trial Chamber is of the opinion that an immediate resolution by the Appeals Chamber may materially advance the proceedings. Apart from quoting these requirements of the Rule, the joint request fails to demonstrate how the impugned decision would significantly affect the fair and expeditious conduct of the proceedings or the outcome of the trial. The argument that the said expert opinion is necessary to establish basic principles of subordination within the JNA in order to explain what the actual positions of the accused were is not sufficient to satisfy the threshold of the Trial Chamber regarding certification under Rule 73(B) of the Rules.
