For the foregoing reasons, the Trial Chamber dismisses the joint request and declines certification. Can we have the next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Good afternoon and please make the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. Please sit down.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, please. These three binders are for the Trial Chamber and that one is for the registry. Your Honours, these are the bundles of the documents that the Defence for Blagoje Simic would like to introduce during the examination of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: One copy for each member of the Trial Chamber, with the specification, also of the documents that will be -- exhibits that were already admitted, so that we can follow the proceedings, and specifically the exhibits. And also we already provided one copy for the -- for the court officer. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. Examined by Mr. Pantelic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Ninkovic.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you hear everything? Can you hear the interpretation? Is everything all right?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please introduce yourself. When were you born, your name and surname, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm Bozo Ninkovic. I was born on the 5th of April, 1959, in Bosanski Samac, Municipality of Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please pause a bit after my question so that the interpreters will have enough time to interpret everything. Thank you. Tell me, what about your family status? Are you married? Have you got any children?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I'm married. I have a wife and two children. I have a nine-year-old daughter and another daughter who is a year and a half old.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your father, his father, your great grandfather, your great, great grandfather? Where are your family roots actually?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: My family roots are from Donja Dubica. This is a village in the municipality of Odzak. That is a neighbouring municipality, as far as Samac is concerned; that is to say, west of Samac. That is where my grandfather and my father were born, as well as my mother.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So approximately at least three or four generations?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They all hail from that area?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Tell me, Mr. Ninkovic, you completed post-secondary school and you have the title of engineer of civilian protection; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During your education, you had a series of subjects related to national defence, civil defence and protection, and all other aspects involved?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, did you do your military service?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did that take place?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you do your military service and in which branch?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: I served in the navy, and I was on a submarine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you get a commission?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I'm a reserve lieutenant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you get your first job?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: I got my first job as a trainee at the Secretariat for National Defence of the Municipal Assembly of Odzak in March 1985.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if I got my math right, you have a total of 17 years of service?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Until when were you in that line of work, military administration, that is?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, this is the way it was: I was in the Secretariat --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, no, no. Until which year? I mean, do you still work in this area?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: No. Until the 25th of May, 2000, I was in the Ministry of Defence. I was involved in defence matters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. So that is a total of 15 years of your service in that area?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, active service in that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, what do you do now? What is your position now?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: Now, I am president of the Municipal Assembly of Samac after the elections that were held in April 2000.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm a bit confused. You are president of the municipal assembly, but we also had Mr. Lukic as a witness, who is mayor of the municipality. Could you explain the two.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: I am president of the local parliament. So there are assemblymen, MPs who are elected in free elections, and Mr. Lukic represents the executive government. So he is the municipal government, to be quite specific, the executive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this chief executive has more in common with a mayor in the west?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I would like to say that the local government in Bosnia-Herzegovina and Republika Srpska were reorganised and from 2000 there has been a new set-up in terms of local government. So the mayor has an important position in terms of budget, appropriation, et cetera. So he has the effective instruments of power.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about your position?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel please not speak at the same time when the witness is speaking.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: The assembly elects the head of the executive, but then also enactments are passed, those that are proposed as bills by the mayor. So the mayor would be elected through direct elections. All citizens who have the right to vote would take part in that vote.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, you are forgetting to pause.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was -- I was actually a little bit ambushed by the testimony of this witness with the speed of his explanation, because I was just about to pose him a question, but I will -- I will --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Let him complete and wait a bit and then you can pose your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ninkovic, just one more question. Actually, as president of the municipal parliament -- I mean, how would you explain that? Is this some kind of a presiding person in parliament? How can we explain this to the Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I as the president of the assembly am at the same time one of the assemblymen. I convene the sessions of the local parliament concerning the programme of work that is adopted once a year, and then we put on the agenda items related to the work of the assembly and I chair that session and I am in charge of that session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell the Trial Chamber, please, something that has to do with your actual line of work, because you worked in the municipal administration for 15 years on defence matters. Did you take a special examination in the administration?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. According to our law on state administration, no one can work in state administration, and anyone with a post-secondary degree or a higher university degree unless they pass a state examination.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me for interrupting. You will continue. I'm sorry. Actually, I'm sorry for interrupting.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: This state examination is passed in the ministry of the judiciary and I passed it in 1989 in Sarajevo. It consists of several tests. The constitution, the system of state administration, then administrative litigation, the law on labour relations, and also office management.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ninkovic, could you please slow down at least a little bit so that they could interpret everything that you are saying into proper English. Please. So can you slow down. So now, this special examination, this professional examination that has to be taken. So that is practically a prerequisite in order to be an official in the administration. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. The administration carries out laws and other regulations, and nobody can work in a certain position if they are not familiar with the law and if they do not know how to interpret the law.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that pertain to administrative procedure as well?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is your knowledge in terms of the military subject matter, if I can put it that way? National defence, et cetera. Do you consider yourself to be an expert, a professional, someone who is well versed in this subject matter?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: I can say that I consider myself to be a person well versed in these matters because for all of these 15 years, I worked on defence matters. So the basic law was the law and the army -- or rather, the law on defence and then the law on the army and then an entire series of various enactments, degrees, by-laws, et cetera, that are based on these laws. Then on civilian protection, on work obligation, and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During your military training, the exercises you did after doing your military service and as a reserve officer, I assume that you acquired some knowledge related to military doctrine, and this narrower aspect. Is that correct? Can you explain this as well.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. As an employee in the Ministry of Defence, like other persons, I went through certain seminars, so we were trained in various fields. Not only in terms of military service but also the entire defence system that was in force in our country.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just tell me a few more things. Namely, your party affiliation. I'm interested in the following: 1990. In 1990, during the multi-party elections in Samac in Bosnia-Herzegovina, what party were you a member of?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: I was a member of the Liberal Party of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and I was a candidate of that party at the parliamentary elections, and I ranked fourth on their list and I was a member of the assembly of that particular political party.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time who was president of your party at the level of all of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: Rasim Kadic, an ethnic Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the municipal parliamentary elections in 1990, did your party achieve certain results? If so, specifically how many seats did you have in the municipal parliament of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did achieve some results. We were a parliamentary party. We had only one seat in parliament, and therefore one assemblyman, namely, Mr. Simeon Simic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please tell me, during 1992 -- MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: It -- I'm not following this portion of the evidence. It may assist you. I don't know. But the witness has said that he was a member of the assembly. He was a candidate of the Liberal Party. He was fourth on the list and he was a member of the assembly of that particular party.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: He then goes on to say that he was -- and the party only had one assemblyman, Mr. Simeon Simic. Am I correct in understanding that he's saying he was -- he was in the assembly of the small political party but not in the municipal assembly? I want to know whether or not he was actually in the assembly, the Municipal Assembly of Bosanski Samac, or not. And I'm not quite sure about the evidence on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The witness will explain that. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: I will clarify.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please do it slowly.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: All right. The Liberal Party had its organs. Therefore, they had the chairman of the party and the assembly of the party. I was a member of that assembly, which is a political body of the party. And this position of mine should not be linked to the local elections for the local assembly. I was candidate for the state assembly at the republic level, and that should be differentiated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, has that clarified the issue? MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 1991, what party were you a member of?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: The same party, the Liberal Party.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about 1992?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: The same.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you a member of the Liberal Party today?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: No. Such party doesn't exist in Republika Srpska. It exists in the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What party are you a member of?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: Now I am a member of the Serb Democratic Party.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, as president of the local municipal assembly, can you tell us what parties are represented in that assembly.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: Local parliament has 25 assemblymen or MPs. There is a total of eight political parties. Let us start from the Serb Democratic Party. Then we have the socialist party of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: This evidence is not helpful. And you've got your summary of what this witness is supposed to discuss.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please tell me, when did you become a member of the SDS, if you are a member of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: That was between 1993 and 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, we shall turn to the period covered by the indictment. So please tell us, what was your occupation in October of 1992? What post did you have then?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: I worked in the Secretariat of National Defence, and I was an official in charge of the -- not in charge. I was an official dealing with civilian protection.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where was that?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: It was in Samac in the Secretariat for National Defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was at the helm of that secretariat?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Milos Bogdanovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please explain to the Trial Chamber what was the role of the Secretariat for People's Defence.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: All right. That is a municipal administrative organ dealing with the people's defence, and it had several activities and tasks. I have to say that the Federal Assembly of the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia in 1991, in April, based on its law exempted the military service from the Secretariat of the People's Defence and transferred it to the military organ, so that in October we dealt with civilian protection with the service on monitoring and reporting. Then on some civilian structures. So these are the matters that we dealt with, whereas the matter that had to do with military service were transferred to the military organs. And these were tasks that had to do with mobilisation, sending of conscripts to various formations, medical exams, and so on. So everything that had to do strictly speaking with the military and mandatory military service.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then you said that in 1991 this was not in the jurisdiction of the Secretariat for People's Defence but, rather, was transferred and became the responsibility of military organs in a certain territory. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Pursuant to that law, these tasks were transferred to the competencies of the military organs. The main staff of the Yugoslav People's Army passed a document which designated a deadline, namely by the 30th of July, 1991, these tasks were to be transferred to the military territorial organs, whereas the commands of the JNA were ordered to establish commands of military districts and military zones so that the military records were supposed to be transferred from the Secretariat for Defence to the military offices. Specifically in Samac, these records were taken from the secretariat and transferred to the military district in Brcko, which was under the Tuzla command. And the -- also, some of the personnel were transferred from the secretariat to the army, where they served as civilians to -- and they served in these military offices as civilian officials. And based on what I know, these people were transferred in August of 1992 and they went to work in the military office in Brcko, so that the secretariat was left only with civilian matters, civilian protection, preparation of civilian population, for defence, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to check the transcript because my colleagues just informed me that there are some inconsistencies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I will check, please. Could you bear with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Maybe -- I apologise. Maybe I can help my colleague Pantelic. I didn't catch quite clearly because frankly the witness is speaking pretty fast. But on line -- on page 100, line 1, he said that in August 1992 it was transferred, and I believe that -- that I heard 1991, but I -- I am not a hundred per cent sure, so I just would like --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. You can clarify that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I will clarify that, yes. Yes, Your Honour. Thank you. Thank you, my dear friend.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ninkovic, please go on slower so that the interpreters can interpret well. Now, let's clarify this. Did you say that the officials from the secretariat went to work in the military office in Brcko in August of 1991?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they did. Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you this: Please bear in mind that everything you and I say has to be interpreted into English. You and I understand each other without any problem, but others need to understand what we're talking about as well. Now, pardon me for this interruption. Now, let us continue. You started telling us how the tasks dealing with civilian protection and the preparation of civilian population organs remained within the responsibilities of the Municipal Secretariat for People's Defence. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, tell me, please, starting in October of 1991, you as a well-educated person, did you have any information about what was going on in the parliamentary life at the level of Bosnia and Herzegovina? Do you have any personal knowledge regarding this and what can you tell us? Just please slowly. MR. DI FAZIO: Your Honours -- if Your Honours please, it's breathtakingly-wide question and an invitation to speculation. If Mr. Pantelic wants to -- and he must know what it is he's interested in -- extract for whatever reason evidence of what happened in the national parliament, then he should be specific and make it clear. But to ask a witness do you have any information about what was going on? Well, no doubt there were lots of things going on in that year in the national parliament and quite apart from that, one wonders how the witness could even begin to answer such a question. So -- but the ultimate result will be speculation if -- if the witness attempts to ask such a wide, broad question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to explore that, because you know this witness was a member of one parliamentary party on the level of the parliament of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Maybe yes, maybe not. We should see whether he's a person -- what is the level of his personal knowledge of the parliamentary life in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But I can be more focussed on that issue. No problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. You need to be specific and ask him what was happening regarding what.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So please be more specific.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, Your Honour. I'll take that. Of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ninkovic, what do you personally know about the events in the parliament of Bosnia and Herzegovina in October of 1991?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: The Liberal Party organs - and I was a member of that party - had various discussions and debates. My party was represented in the parliament, and we in the party participated in those events. At that time, parties that held power were the SDA, HDZ, and the SDS. However, their relationship was quite bad and there were frequent conflicts and interruptions in the work of the parliament. There were reactions, fierce reactions from members of parliament, and so on. What needs to be said here before this Trial Chamber is that at the time a decision was passed on holding a referendum, according to which the citizens were to say whether they favoured remaining in the existing Yugoslavia or they supported an independent Bosnia and Herzegovina. Regarding that, there was a very active debate held; however, representatives, members of the SDA and HDZ in that procedure outvoted the representatives of the SDS and some other parties, those parties that were Serb parties. So the referendum was scheduled, but the Serbs did not participate in that referendum. I will now remind you of the constitution of Bosnia and Herzegovina, which --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: -- Intervention to the transcript. Page 103, line 3. He said, "Those parties that were Serb parties." This is not what the witness stated. He said that the members of the parliament from other parties of Serb origin. It -- it is not the same thing, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I will clarify that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before we get to that period, please tell us this: What do you know -- or do you know that in October of 1991 in the republic parliament of BH the Serb members of the parliament left that parliament? Do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. A lot of citizens of Bosnia-Herzegovina know about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that broadcast in the media?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was. I have to say that the events in the parliament were covered very well in the media, newspapers, television, and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to ask you something else. After October 1991, do you know whether in the first half of November 1991 a plebiscite of Serb people in Bosnia and Herzegovina was held?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot remember the exact date; however, I know that a plebiscite was held, at which the Serbs voted in favour of remaining in SFRY.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please tell me this: When did you hear for the first time about the republic of the Serbian people in Bosnia-Herzegovina? Let's call it briefly -- shortly Republika Srpska? When did you first hear of its establishment?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: It was between 1991 and 1992. I can't give you the exact date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you personally know about organisational structure of the Croatian people in Bosnia and Herzegovina? Did they have their own entities?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: I live in Posavina. I lived in the municipality of Odzak. I worked in the municipality of Samac, so this is all called Posavina region, and I know that in this region, which covers several municipalities - Bosanski Brod, Derventa, Odzak, Modrica, Bosanski Samac, Orasje - I know that the Croatian Democratic Union had some activities that were aimed at establishing Bosnian Posavina, which is a territorial entity in that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you learn first about such a territorial organisation? MR. DI FAZIO: Well, if Your Honours please, I object to this evidence on the grounds of relevance. The creation of -- sorry, the creation of Croatian entities during the period of time in the -- covered by the indictment is not relevant to the events that you have to deal with, unless in some way it directly is concerned with the -- similar SDS entities. The fact that it may have been going on, that other Croatian organs and bodies may have been created, that there were such activities going on, is not -- can't be relevant to the issues that you have to deal with, namely the creation of the parallel organs, Serb-only organs and so on. And it's -- at the end of the day if you hear this evidence and digest it, how sit going to assist you with those particular issues? Time is running and the greater the time consumed in the examination-in-chief, the greater the Prosecution to complete its cross-examination, so it affecting the Prosecution directly. There's got to be some sort of relevance to these particular topics being raised by Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, sorry. Your Honour, everything is to some extent relevant, especially for the region of Posavina. How three ethnic groups were organised, finally divided, what are the consequences. So it's just a -- an introductory, I would say, topic from the point of view of the personal knowledge of this witness and then we are going to the region because he's -- he said that he lived in Odzak, which is covered by the indictment. He worked in Samac, which is covered by the indictment. This witness can give us some details about his life in -- by the end of 1991.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. There is some relevance in the sense that we are dealing with allegations of forcible takeover, so we need to know who was actually controlling which territory at the material time. But do be brief, instead of giving us too much detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour. It was not my intention to go into big details. It's absolutely enough.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ninkovic, what is your personal knowledge as a person with military experience with regard to the fact that you travel extensively from Odzak to Samac? So can you please tell me something about the atmosphere which prevailed among the different ethnic groups in the region of Odzak in late 1991 up to April 1992? What did you personally notice in your region where you lived?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: The situation was very difficult, characterised by a number of incidents of political and armed nature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please slow down.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: So it was a period of crisis characterised by a number of incidents ranging from political incidents to armed clashes. So that period -- that region is in the immediate vicinity of the Sava River and across the Sava River is the Republic of Croatia, which was at war at the time. So it was a period marked by the formation of paramilitary groups, and the only regular military formation was the JNA. And Croats and Muslims mostly led by their respective parties - that is, the SDA and the HDZ - at that period intensively were engaged in establishing their paramilitary formations in Bosanski Brod, Modrica, Odzak, Derventa, Bosanski Samac, and Orasje municipalities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ninkovic, you've mentioned some incidents and you also said that there were armed clashes. Can you please explain for the Chamber what it was all about on the basis of some examples of the incidents which happened in late 1991 up to April 1992. What type of incidents were those? Who participated in them? And what was their nature? Can you illustrate a bit in a bit more detail.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: I can tell you something about the most important incident, which was not an incident as such. It was at the moment when the regular forces from the Republic of Croatia stormed on the axis from Slavonski Brod to Bosanski Brod. It was in March 1992. So the regular armed forces of the Republic of Croatia entered Bosnia and Herzegovina in the area of Bosanski Brod municipality. Several Serbian villages were set aflame at the time and several civilians were killed in Sijekovac, which resulted in a deadly fear among the Serbian population. So this was the incident which was a turning point for the future events. There are some other minor incidents, minor armed clashes. I'm going to mention a few such incidents that happened in Samac. One was when a hand grenade was thrown into a cafe bar in Samac. I believe that one person was killed and another person was seriously injured. There was another incident in the green market in the same town. What happened was a man who was of pro Yugoslav affiliation, but he was a Muslim, he was shot at in the afternoon. I believe his name was Ramusovic. And on the 21st of March, there was -- the town was blocked by Muslims who put up barricades and nobody could enter Samac. I remember that it was Saturday, and I took my mother to the green market. It was customary for everybody to go to the market on Saturday mornings, and I couldn't cross the bridge from Dubica. I couldn't enter Samac because there were barricades on the roads. Obviously there were a number of checkpoints. I travelled from my house in Dubica to my workplace in Samac. This is a distance of some 9 kilometres. Dubica is a Serbian village, and there is another village on the road to Samac, a Croatian village, called Prud. I was stopped there very often. I was stopped by uniformed men carrying arms, and judging by their accent, by the way they spoke, they were not local Croats. They were people from Croatia, more specifically from Slavonia. Usually the local Croat population wore masks on their heads so that we wouldn't recognise them. There were also reserve police checkpoints on the bridge composed of Muslims and Croats, but they didn't create any major problems to the population.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned Prud. Can you tell me whether Prud was territorially a part of Samac municipality.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is Prud west of Samac across the Bosna River?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, in Prud, did you notice any armed formations?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, particularly during the period from late February to March and the beginning of April.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How would you describe those formations?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: Those were armed people, armed men wearing camouflage uniforms. They were members of the ZNG, which was at the time the official army of the Republic of Croatia. They would stop vehicles, people. They would ask for their identity papers. They would search the cars, open the cars, and they would ask people whether they were Croats or Muslims or what.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any personal knowledge when we're talking about the period between late 1991 and April 1992 of the cases of physical liquidation, that is, the killing of the Serbian leaders of the Posavina region?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: I learnt about those things from unofficial sources, and I learnt that such things happened in Bosanski Brod, but I never saw any official reports on any of such events.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ninkovic, in Odzak municipality in April 1992, do you have any personal knowledge which of the political parties were in power in Odzak municipality?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: The Croatian Democratic Union had a leading position. They held a position of the president of the municipal assembly, the Chief of the Public Security Station. Then there was also the Party of the Democratic action. I believe that they held the sectors of economy and the communal system, I believe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you first learn about the arrests and crimes committed with the Serbian population in Odzak?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: War had already started in that area. I would just like to say that before the war, there were checkpoints. Serbs from Dubica and Trnjak, which is another neighbouring village, could not go to Samac because there were some problems at the checkpoints and that instilled fear among people and villagers of Trnjak and Dubica asked for a meeting with the leadership of Odzak municipality, because people were rather, especially after the events which had taken place in Brod. At a meeting which was held in Voskova village, which was between Trnjak and Dubica, there were representatives of Odzak municipality and there were some Serbs, amongst whom I was also there. And there was some discussions about dealing with the -- all these things in a peaceful way. However, it was Ivica Matanovic, who gave the tone to that meeting. He introduced himself as an HVO commander who joined the HVO from the JNA. I believe that he was in the garrison of the JNA in Slavonska Pozega, he was rather edgy and he even voiced some threats from time to time. And he said that the Serbs did not respond to the mobilisation calls by the JNA, and he also said the JNA was not a regular army, that it was the aggressor army. He also said that it was an armed force which was not desirable in that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what would be the consequence if the Serbs did not listen to him? What consequences would the Serbs suffer?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: He said that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The evidence now being adduced in detail is not relevant to the indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And looking at your summary, we have completed the ethnic tensions between the parties, between the people, and what was happening in the Posavina municipalities. We should now move over.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I'm just moving to the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: To the remain --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: To April and May 1992. That is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. On the establishment of the Municipal Crisis Staff. We'll start on these issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any personal knowledge, Mr. Ninkovic, of the existence of the Crisis Staff in Odzak?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. I didn't understand your question. I had noise in my earphones. Can you repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ninkovic, do you have any personal knowledge of the existence of the Crisis Staff in Odzak?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell us what you know about it.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: I already said that this period was marked by the establishment of Bosanska Posavina and that the key role in the establishment of that territorial organisation of Bosnian Croats was played by the Crisis Staffs, which had been formed by the Croatian Democratic Union.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any Serbs in the Crisis Staff in Odzak?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We aren't discussing the Croatian institutions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No, no. Absolutely not. I'm just speaking about the territorial aspect of the indictment, Odzak, and then the -- because I don't have any other, frankly, witness who can shed light on that issue, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. This witness, according to your summaries, is dealing with the Municipal Crisis Staff in the Samac municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. And in atmosphere in neighbouring municipality, which is Odzak. That was the -- that was the issue. It's a part of the indictment, in fact. MR. DI FAZIO: Well, if Your Honours please, I think this illustrates my earlier point. Number one, territorial aspect of the indictment of Odzak -- in Odzak. There is no explanation of what territorial aspect means. Atmosphere in the neighbouring municipality which is Odzak, it's difficult to see how that is such a broad term, the atmosphere is relevant in any -- in any way at all. With respect, Mr. Pantelic has to be more specific and more precise in his selection of topics to -- upon which to illicit evidence from this particular witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, Your Honour. In fact, this is a part of the summary of this witness related to the other factual allegations from the indictment. It's paragraph 9 of the indictment. So I have to defend my client to the best extent that I can with a certain number of evidences. First of all, I would like to explore from the personal knowledge of this witness who was in charge in April 1992 in Odzak, which is a neighbouring municipality and which is covered by the indictment. And then I'm going to the -- chronologically I'm going to the other events, Your Honour. And that's why I'm asking him what is his personal knowledge of the Crisis Staff of Odzak, of the members of that Crisis Staff and certain events on the territory or in Odzak in April 1992, Your Honour. That is the basis of my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ninkovic, do you have any personal knowledge of firstly the time when the Crisis Staff of Odzak was established?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: It was during the period between -- in March.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if there were any Serb representatives in the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't have any personal knowledge of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you first learn about the arrests of the Serbian civilians in the territory of Odzak municipality, and how many of them were arrested and what happened to them?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: Before the beginning of war in that area, there were arrests. So when a Serb would come to the checkpoint, there were verbal threats, abuses, and then some would be taken for an interrogation, and then they would be released. But that -- all of those things instilled fear among the local population, and people started moving out towards safer areas. Some of them even took all their property with them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When exactly did you learn about Serb civilians being arrested for the first time in the territory of Odzak municipality, if you can remember the time when you heard that?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: There were sporadic incidents of that sort in March and April.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any mass, large-scale arrests?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That was on the 8th of May, when a number -- a large number of Serbs were put in a very difficult position. I believe that we're talking about some 3.000 people in Novi Grad, Dubica, and Trnjak. These are Serb villages in that area, in the territory of Odzak municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are we talking about the year 1992? Because you mentioned the 8th of May.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's what we're talking about, the year 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened to these people?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: These people were isolated. They were put in prisons. They were put under arrest. These were people who were able-bodied men, fit for military service, and they were put in prison.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the place where that was?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, in Odzak. It was in the school and at various other places like Strolit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is Strolit?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: Strolit is a metallurgy factory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: When you said that you wanted to discuss Odzak, it was only in relation to who was in charge. And then we move on to the Samac municipality, which we're dealing with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. But I already --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: None of the defendants are answering allegations that they did anything to the Serbs in Odzak.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I've finished with this line of questioning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The crimes which your clients are facing are quite clear, so you stop wasting time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That will be cut down from the -- the submitted time for your examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. That was the end -- virtually that was the last question in this line of questioning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tell me, Mr. Ninkovic, what was the situation in your Secretariat for National Defence in Samac? In the period between 1991 and 1992, who were the employees of that secretariat? You already said that the late Mr. Bogdanovic was secretariat of the secretariat. Can you explain to the Trial Chamber what the atmosphere was within your secretariat in Samac.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Well, you know, like in other organs and institutions at that time there were these inter-ethnic tensions; that is to say, that every employee who worked there in a way had a political point of view stemming from the ethnic community it belonged to. That was not only characteristic of the secretariat. That's the way it was in the police, in the municipal agencies, various inspectorates, financial services, the public utility services, et cetera. So there was a situation along ethnic lines among people. And they defined their position on the basis of the dominant views within the ethnic community they belonged to and the political parties they were affiliated with. So this was a time of turmoil, tensions ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anybody from any political party exercise any kind of control over the secretariat at that time? If so, can you tell us more specifically who this was.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: In the secretariat there were people from various parties, from the HDZ, from the SDP, from the Liberal Party. There were people who were not in any political party but who did have certain political views of their own and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you heard of the Hundzar Division?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What can you tell us about this?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC
utterances.text: This goes back to the time of the Second World War. These were actually the elite units of the Muslim who is belonged to the Ustasha --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Why are you discussing this?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Because I would like to ask this witness about the Exhibit D --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can you move to your summary. Can you look at your summary for this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. If you look from the beginning, we've covered the political situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We've covered the relation between the SDS --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: -- and the other parties. We've covered activities, checkpoints, armaments, and the incidents.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Inter-ethnic tension between three groups.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We have done that. You can read through the transcript. We should now start with establishment of Municipal Crisis Staff. And this is in Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But I have some documents admitted in the Prosecution case which I would like now to discuss with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Regarding what?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Reporting his personal knowledge of the existence of certain documents. Maybe he -- he is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Which ones? Which ones?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. You can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And my question is to ask him whether he saw this exhibit, in which form, when and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. That, you can go ahead. But we are not interested in history.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I'm going, yes, to show this exhibit to the witness. But Your Honour, to be frank, maybe we could do that -- because it's -- it's about time for our adjournment, so I -- why should we -- I don't believe that we shall have enough time to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well. We'll continue on Friday.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And we'll stick to the summaries.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I'm now going into the presentation of exhibits already admitted and then this new, well, potential Defence exhibits which are in this bundle. So we'll go through this, of course.
